v: For wisdom will enter into your heart. Knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
b: In this passage God calls each person to bury wisdom deep in our hearts. Wisdom does not refer only to knowledge and understanding in the mind, but to a beautiful virtue and inner values. It is the compass of our lives, guiding us to make right choices and actions.

So how can we let wisdom enter our hearts? Just as a garden needs tilling and watering, our hearts also need to be cared for and cultivated. First, we should keep learning and pursuing knowledge. By reading the Bible, praying and fellowshipping with spiritual companions, we can gain heavenly wisdom. Second, we need to keep a humble attitude and be willing to accept instruction and guidance. Only when we learn humbly can we truly grasp the value of wisdom.

There was a young farmer. He had always worked hard at farming, but he could not find a way to solve the problems with his crops. He despaired and felt he knew nothing. So he went to an old farmer for help. The old farmer told him to observe the soil and plants carefully and to learn farming skills. The young farmer followed the old farmer’s advice and began to learn and apply this knowledge. In the end, his crops grew strong and he had an abundant harvest.

This story tells us that as long as we are willing to learn and accept the guidance of wisdom, we can succeed in life. Whether at work, in the family or in relationships, wisdom can help us make wise decisions. It lets us keep away from misunderstanding and conflict, and brings harmony and peace.
Dear family, let us pursue God’s will every day with a heart that longs for wisdom. When we place wisdom in our hearts, our lives will be filled with love for God and care for others.
a: Seek God’s word: Spend time each day reading the Bible and meditating on God’s word. Take part in the church’s Bible study groups or gatherings, and share what you learn with other brothers and sisters. When you meet difficulty or doubt in life, pray to God for wisdom.
Pursue knowledge: Stay curious, read more and learn more. Take part actively in various learning and training activities. Cultivate good study habits and raise your learning efficiency.
Live out a life of wisdom: Make wise choices in life. Guide your words and conduct with God’s word. Help others and spread wisdom.
pr:
Dear Jesus, give us hearts of wisdom, that we may understand Your will and live lives that glorify You.
Help us to spend time each day reading the Bible and meditating on Your word, drawing wisdom and strength from it.
Guide us to pursue knowledge, keep learning and growing, and benefit others with wisdom.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain abundant wisdom and peace on your journey of pursuing wisdom. Amen.

t: Filled with the Spirit of Wisdom
v: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. The children of Israel listened to him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses.
b: In this verse we see Moses passing the spirit of wisdom to Joshua, making him the leader of God’s chosen people, Israel. This leader, full of wisdom, led the Israelites onto the right path; they obeyed God’s commands and did what God required.

This story tells us that when we are filled with wisdom, we can become vessels of God, influencing and leading others onto the right path. Wisdom is not only knowledge and understanding; it is also an ability that goes beyond common sense and intuition, the ability to form right judgments and make wise decisions.

In our lives we often face all kinds of difficulties and choices. Sometimes we may feel lost and confused, not knowing how to act. But when we seek and receive God’s wisdom, we can obtain supernatural guidance and strength to help us make wise choices in hardship.

Like Joshua, when we are filled with wisdom, our words and actions will show God’s wisdom and guidance. Our lives will become a testimony that draws others to seek God’s truth and wisdom. As long as we are willing to lay down our pride and self-assurance and seek God’s will, He will surely give us wisdom and guidance.

So let us come humbly before God every day, longing for His wisdom and guidance. When we face choices and difficulties, let us not rely on our own wisdom but on God’s wisdom. When we become people filled with wisdom, we will become vessels of God, leading others onto the right path.
a: Seek the filling of the Holy Spirit: Spend time in prayer every day, asking to be filled with the Holy Spirit. Take an active part in the church’s worship and praise, and let the Holy Spirit move our hearts. When you meet difficulty or temptation in life, rely on the Holy Spirit’s power to overcome.

Pursue spiritual wisdom: Besides reading the Bible, read more devotional books and sermons, and learn spiritual knowledge. Join the church’s Bible classes or training courses and keep growing spiritually. Talk with mature Christians and learn from them.
Live out a life of wisdom: Make choices in life that accord with God’s heart. Guide your words and conduct by the Holy Spirit’s leading. Serve others with spiritual wisdom, glorifying God.
pr:
Dear Holy Spirit, fill us and give us wisdom and strength, that we may understand God’s will and live a life that glorifies God.
Help us to spend time in prayer each day, seeking Your filling, so that our lives are full of Your power and wisdom.
Guide us to pursue spiritual wisdom, keep learning and growing, and benefit others with wisdom.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you seek God’s wisdom every day and become His witness. Amen.

v: All Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to do justice.
b: In this verse we see the people of Israel standing in awe of King Solomon’s judgment. Why? Because they saw that the wisdom of God was in his heart, to do justice.

We also need to understand how precious God’s wisdom is! As Proverbs says, “She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her.” (Proverbs 3:15) God’s wisdom is not merely knowledge in the head, but a divine gift that surpasses human wisdom.

In our daily lives we also need God’s wisdom. Sometimes we may face a choice and not know what to do. Or we may meet difficulties and challenges and not know how to solve them. But we can trust God’s wisdom and ask Him to give us guidance and wise judgment.

A man met a hard problem between work and family and did not know what to choose. He was very confused and felt pressure and anxiety. But he decided to pray, entrusting his difficulty to God and asking Him for wisdom. After praying, he received an unexpected phone call and was offered a job opportunity. This opportunity not only matched his education and skills, but, more importantly, would let him balance family and work. He saw God’s wisdom at work in his life, and felt very humble and grateful.

So when we face choices and difficulties, let us not rely on our own wisdom, but humbly seek God’s wisdom and guidance. God’s wisdom surpasses our understanding, but He is willing to give it to us, so that we may have faith, hope and love in life.
ah: 1 Kings 3:28 records that the Israelites stood in awe of King Solomon because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him. In daily life we too should long for and pursue the wisdom God gives:
a: Pray often for God’s wisdom, and when facing hard questions first ask for God’s will.
Read the Bible humbly and meditate on it, absorb the teaching of God’s wisdom in the Bible, and apply it in life.
Think three times before you act on decisions, and use wisdom to weigh gains and losses.
Handle relationships with wisdom, be considerate and tolerant, and maintain peaceful relations.
Manage your life with wisdom, set priorities, and overcome procrastination and excess.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us heavenly wisdom, so that we can live in line with Your heart. Make us pray often for Your wisdom, always learn humbly from the Bible’s teaching, and apply all the wisdom we receive in life. Bless us to weigh matters carefully and make wise decisions, to handle relationships with wisdom and live in peace with people. Also give us wisdom to manage our lives and overcome weakness, and live by Your will. We are willing to fear You and rely wholeheartedly on Your wisdom, which goes beyond what people can reach. We pray in the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you seek God’s wisdom in every choice and difficulty and receive His guidance. Amen.

v: God gave Solomon abundant wisdom, understanding, and breadth of mind like the sand that is on the seashore.
b: Solomon was one of the wisest kings in the history of Israel. He prayed to God, asking Him to give him wisdom to govern the nation, and God granted his request. This passage reveals God’s generous gift of wisdom, and inspires us through the story.

One day two mothers came before Solomon, arguing over the ownership of a baby. Both claimed the baby was her own, and there was no evidence to prove who the real mother was. Solomon faced a difficult decision, but his wisdom led him to make a startling proposal: cut the child in two and give half to each mother.

When the other mother heard this terrible verdict, she cried out at once and begged for mercy. She was willing to give up the child, asking only to protect the baby’s life. When Solomon heard this mother’s plea, he knew immediately who the real mother was. He ordered the child to be given to this mother, to protect the child’s life and well-being.

This story tells us that wisdom is not only a sharp mind, but comes from God’s revelation. When Solomon faced difficulty, God gave him wisdom beyond that of ordinary people, able to discern the truth and make a just judgment. This wisdom enabled him to protect an innocent life and show God’s great love and justice.

In our lives we also need wisdom to face all kinds of difficulties and choices. Sometimes we may meet choices like Solomon’s, needing wisdom to make the right decision. But we need not worry, because God’s wisdom is without end, immeasurable like the sand of the sea.

When we face difficulty, let us pray to God and ask Him to give us wisdom. He is willing to walk with us and guide us onto the right road. Believe that God’s wisdom will bring us faith and hope, because He knows what is the best road for us.

Today, let us remember this story and ask God to give us wisdom like Solomon’s. May God’s wisdom guide us to make right decisions, protect our lives and the lives of others, and show us the right direction in life.
ah: 1 Kings 4:29 shows us that God gave Solomon exceedingly great wisdom and understanding and breadth of heart. As God’s people, we too should pursue the wisdom God gives:
a: Often meditate on God’s word in devotions, receive the wisdom of the Bible, and make the heart as broad as a sea of sand.
In life, observe and appreciate more of God’s wonderful works, and increase your knowledge and reverence of God’s wisdom.
Humbly consult those who have spiritual wisdom, and draw on their understanding of the truth.
Discern right from wrong with wisdom, conduct yourself according to God’s will, and do not follow worldly standards.
Spread the gospel with wisdom, bear witness to God’s great power, and influence the people around you to turn to Christ.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving exceedingly great wisdom and understanding; may we all, like Solomon, have a breadth of heart like the sand of the sea. Make us often think on the wisdom of Your word, and revere You as we appreciate Your wonderful works. Also give us humble hearts that long for truth, willing to consult spiritual elders and keep absorbing the wisdom of others. Let us discern right from wrong with wisdom, conduct ourselves according to Your heart, and glorify You with lives of wisdom. We pray in the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. When you meet difficulty in life, may you take God’s wisdom as your guide and embrace every decision with God’s love and justice. Amen.

v: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
b: This passage reminds us that the author of the book complacently declares that he has gained great wisdom, surpassing others. But can we really obtain true happiness and success through wisdom and knowledge?

A young and talented scholar was learned and exceptionally wise, and was famous in the city. He thought he had already obtained everything, and regarded his wisdom and knowledge as the only way to success.

One day he met a humble old man. The old man saw through his pride and vanity and said to him, “My child, wisdom and knowledge can make you successful in the eyes of the world, but true happiness and success come from inner harmony and love. If you pursue only worldly wisdom, you will lose the ability to connect with others, and lose the chance to understand, care for and help them.”

The young scholar was deeply shaken when he heard the old man’s words. He began to reflect on his motives in pursuing wisdom, and realized that he lacked love and care for others. So he decided to readjust his values and put love first.

He began to build relationships with others on his own initiative, caring about their needs and offering help. He found that in the process of connecting with others he learned more wisdom and knowledge, and experienced deeper growth.

This story tells us that wisdom and knowledge alone may make us look successful in the eyes of the world, but true happiness and success are built on love and connection with others. Only when we are willing to care for others and put love first can we gain true wisdom and growth.

So let us strive every day to pursue and practice love, to connect with others, and on that basis to learn more wisdom and knowledge. In this way we will experience richer blessing and success in life.
a: Pursue knowledge: Knowledge is the foundation of wisdom. Only by constant learning and accumulating knowledge can we gain wisdom. Pursuing knowledge requires us to stay curious and to read and learn more. Pursuing knowledge requires us to take an active part in various learning and training activities and keep raising our level of knowledge. Practical ways: spend time every day reading books, magazines, news and so on to broaden your knowledge. Take an active part in the church’s Bible classes and training courses to learn biblical and theological knowledge. Observe and think in life, and draw wisdom from everyday life.

Experience life: Wisdom comes not only from books but from the experience of life. Only by constantly experiencing life can we gain true wisdom. Experiencing life requires us to face challenges bravely and learn lessons from failure. Experiencing life requires us to learn humbly from the experience of others and draw nourishment from their wisdom. Practical ways: take an active part in social activities and exercise your abilities in practice. Be bold to try new things and gain new experiences and insights from them. Talk more with wise people and learn life experience from them.

Fear God: The fear of God is the foundation of wisdom; only by fearing God can we walk on the right path. Fearing God makes us careful in word and deed and keeps us from wrong choices. Fearing God gives us strength to resist temptation and hold fast to our faith. Practical ways: keep God’s teaching in life and do what pleases God. When you meet difficulty or temptation, look to God and rely on God. Serve God with a heart that fears God, and glorify God.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, give us hearts that pursue knowledge, and help us keep learning and accumulating wisdom.
Help us keep experiencing life, drawing wisdom from experience, and living a life that glorifies You.
Give us hearts that fear You, so that we can keep Your teaching and walk on the right path.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you always keep humility and love on the road of pursuing wisdom, and help others with love. Amen.

v: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
b: In this verse God calls the lazy to observe the ant and receive the revelation of wisdom from it. Ants are diligent creatures; they work hard, store food and prepare for winter. They have no habit of laziness or procrastination, but are full of perseverance and steadfastness. This attitude and behavior of the ant is something we can learn from.

In our lives we are often tempted by laziness. When we feel sleepy or unmotivated, it is easy to fall into a lazy state. Yet God reminds us in this verse that only by working hard can we gain wisdom and achievement. Like the ant, we should cultivate perseverance and steadfastness and strive to pursue our goals.

At the same time, this verse also reminds us to value time. Ants know how to treasure every minute and second and use it to do meaningful things. We should also make good use of time like ants, avoiding procrastination and waste. When we see time as a precious resource, we can manage our lives more effectively and achieve our goals.

So let us learn wisdom from the ant. Let us cast off a lazy attitude and let diligence and perseverance bring change to our lives. Let us make good use of time, focus on our goals, and pursue growth and achievement within God’s will.
a: Work diligently: Ants work diligently and are never lazy; they store up grain for winter and prepare for the future. We should learn the ants’ spirit, work diligently and not give up easily. At work, do your best and strive to fulfill your duty. Practical ways: get up on time every day, go to bed early and rise early, and form good habits of daily life. Work conscientiously and responsibly, without procrastinating or being perfunctory. When facing difficulties and challenges, do not give up easily, but persevere.

Prepare ahead: Ants prepare ahead, storing up food in summer for winter. We should learn the ants’ wisdom, having foresight and planning. In life, plan well and prepare for the future. Practical ways: make reasonable study and work plans and strive to carry them out. Save some money for a rainy day. Learn some new skills to prepare for future development.

Teamwork: Ants are social creatures; they unite and cooperate to complete tasks together. We should learn the ants’ spirit, working together and helping and loving one another. In life, cooperate with others to achieve goals together. Practical ways: in a team, be glad to help others and take on responsibility actively. Respect others’ opinions and keep good communication with others. When you meet difficulty, ask others for help.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, give us hearts that work diligently, so that we can work hard and create value for ourselves and others.
Help us prepare ahead, having foresight and planning, and be ready for the future.
Give us a spirit of teamwork, so that we can live in harmony with others and accomplish our goals together.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you learn wisdom from the ant and gain success through hard work. May you make good use of every minute and second and become the person God envisioned. Amen.

v: Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for your commandments are always with me.
b: In this passage we see the psalmist praising God’s commandments, because they are not only always in his heart, but make him wiser than his enemies. This reminds us that obeying God’s word is the key to gaining true wisdom.

In our lives we often meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties, which trouble us like enemies. Yet when we keep God’s commandments in our hearts and take them as our guide, we can rise above these troubles and gain wisdom beyond the world’s.

Like a small boat sailing on the vast sea, meeting huge waves and storms. If the captain has no rudder and no compass, he cannot determine the way forward and cannot overcome adversity. In the same way, if we do not have God’s word as our guide, we too will lose our way in life and not find a true goal.

King David met many difficulties and enemies when he was young. Yet he always remembered God’s commandments, and kept God’s word in his heart. In this way he could stay calm in danger and face his enemies with wisdom and courage.

Once David was challenged by Goliath, a powerful and cruel giant. He faced the giant’s contempt and threats, but he knew God’s commandments were in his heart and that his wisdom came from God. So he rose to the fight without hesitation and defeated the giant with an ordinary stone. This story tells us that when we hold fast to God’s word, we will be wiser and braver than any enemy.

So let us keep writing God’s word on our hearts and let it be the guide of our lives. When we face difficulty, let us believe that these words will give us wisdom and strength, so that we rise above our enemies and overcome challenges.
a: Hide God’s word in your heart: The psalmist hid God’s word in his heart, and so he was wiser than his enemies. We should follow the psalmist’s example and hide God’s word in our hearts. Hiding God’s word in our hearts requires us to spend time reading the Bible and meditating, and to make God’s word part of our own life. Practical ways: spend time reading the Bible every day and memorize some verses. Meditate on God’s word and apply it to real life. When you meet difficulty or temptation, remind yourself with God’s word, to help you make choices that accord with God’s heart.

Keep God’s word: God’s word is the source of wisdom; only by keeping God’s word can we gain true wisdom. Keeping God’s word requires us to live according to God’s heart and do what pleases God. Keeping God’s word helps us avoid wrong choices and walk on the right path. Practical ways: keep God’s teaching in life, such as honoring parents, loving your neighbor as yourself, and being honest and trustworthy. When you meet a hard problem, seek God’s heart rather than acting on your own temper. Use God’s word to help others, to share the gospel and bear witness to God.

Rely on God’s strength: The enemy tries to lure us away from God, but only by relying on God’s strength can we resist the enemy’s schemes. Relying on God’s strength requires us to pray earnestly and seek God’s help. God’s strength can help us overcome difficulties and defeat the enemy. Practical ways: spend time in prayer every day, asking God to give strength. When you meet difficulty or temptation, look to God and rely on God. Trust in God with faith, believing that God will surely help us win.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, help us to hide Your word in our hearts, keep Your word, and rely on Your strength.
Give us hearts of wisdom, that we may understand Your will and walk on the right path.
Keep us by Your great power, help us resist the enemy’s schemes, and gain final victory.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you hold fast to God’s commandments every day and gain wisdom and courage from them. Amen.

v: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
b: In this passage God reveals to us the secrets of wisdom. Wisdom is a precious gift God has given us; it can guide us to make right choices and face the tests of life. Wisdom helps us understand God’s will and saves us from sin.

Like a ship sailing on the sea, wisdom is the helmsman, guiding us to find the right direction. When we face difficulties and challenges, wisdom lets us think calmly and make wise choices. Wisdom also lets us see the consequences of sin and stay pure and upright in conduct.

Let us imagine a person facing the choice between cheating and honesty. If he chooses to cheat, he may gain some benefit in the short term, but in the long run he will lose his conscience and reputation. But if he chooses honesty, although he may face some difficulty in the short term, in the long run he will gain true success and happiness. This is the blessing and benefit that wisdom brings.

We should also understand that even when we make mistakes and sin, God still loves us and is willing to win back our hearts. He does not want to punish us, but to guide us back to the right path. In His rich grace we can find forgiveness and the opportunity to be born anew.

So let us seek wisdom every day and let God teach us all kinds of knowledge. When we face a choice, let us stop and think, ask for God’s will, and make a choice that accords with His heart. Only so can we experience the blessing and benefit that wisdom brings.
ah: 1. Pray daily: Humbly ask God to reveal to us the secrets of heavenly wisdom, and let His wisdom guide us to understand the truth. 2. Go deeper into the Bible: Learn humbly the teaching of wisdom in God’s word, read the Bible quietly every day, and let the revelation of the Bible enter deep into the heart. 3. Observe life: Observe the course of life, look in it for God’s wonderful works and wise arrangements, and record each day in a journal or notebook what moves you and what you realize. 4. Share testimony: Pay attention to receiving the testimonies shared by spiritual companions, take part in small group gatherings or devotional activities, draw on others’ understanding of the truth, and share your own insights with them. 5. Practice the truth: Put into practice the wisdom you receive, live a life that accords with God’s heart, reflect each day on your conduct and attitude, take God’s wisdom as your guide, and glorify God’s name.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for promising to show us the secrets of wisdom. Give us humble hearts, always praying humbly to You, and receiving the revelation and guidance You give. May we listen attentively to the teaching of wisdom in Your word, and let the secrets of truth go deep into our hearts. Let us also see Your wonderful works and wisdom in the course of life, and from them understand more of the secrets of truth. Help us pay attention to the testimonies shared by brothers and sisters, building one another up and gaining wisdom. Finally, grant that we may practice what we have received, live a life in line with the truth, and glorify Your great wisdom with our lives. We pray in the holy name of the Lord Jesus, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you seek wisdom every day and receive the wisdom and guidance God gives. Amen.

v: The mouth of the righteous talks of wisdom. His tongue speaks justice.
b: This verse reminds us that as believers we should influence the world with words of wisdom and fairness. The words we speak have the power to change other people’s lives and to pass on God’s truth.

There was a man named Chengping who had a mouth full of wisdom and fairness. Every time he spoke of wisdom, his words were full of hope and love. He inspired people with parables and stories, letting them see the beauty and potential in life.

One day Chengping met a disappointed and despairing young man, who felt discouraged and did not know how to go on living. Chengping sat down and began to speak of wisdom. He told the young man a parable: “Imagine you are a seed buried in the soil. You must go through darkness and pressure before you can sprout and grow. Just as trees need water and sunlight, in hard times we also need to seek God’s help and guidance.”

After hearing Chengping’s words, the young man felt a surge of new hope and courage. He began to rethink his situation and to believe that he could overcome his difficulties. Soon afterward he found a job and began to build his future.

This story tells us that each of us has the ability to influence others. As long as we speak about life with words of wisdom and fairness, we can give others faith, hope and love. When we inspire others with parables and stories, we can help them see the beauty and possibilities in life.

Let us decide from today to be the righteous whose mouths talk of wisdom and whose tongues speak justice. Let us treat the people around us with words full of faith, hope and love. Whether in the family, at work or in the community, let us speak in a wise way and influence others’ lives.
ah: 1. Consistency of word and deed: Strive to make our words and actions consistent, so that our mouths are as full of wisdom and fairness as our conduct. 2. Wise speech: In daily conversation choose wise words, avoid offending and hurting others, and treat others with wisdom and kindness. 3. Teach others: Use our words to teach others, sharing God’s wisdom and truth, to help them grow in faith and life. 4. Have a just heart: Keep an impartial attitude and mind, show favoritism to no one, and treat everyone by a standard of fairness. 5. Examine our words and deeds: Regularly examine our words and deeds, making sure that what our mouths speak is wisdom and fairness, and keep pursuing progress.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the promise of wisdom. Help our mouths to speak of wisdom, and make our words full of fairness and love. Give us a wise attitude, so that in daily life we glorify Your name with our words. Help us always to examine our words and deeds, making sure that what our mouths say accords with Your heart. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be a righteous person whose mouth talks of wisdom and whose tongue speaks justice. May your words bring others faith, hope and love. Amen.

v: For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold.
b: In this world, we are often drawn to the pursuit of money and wealth. We spend enormous amounts of time and energy chasing riches, while neglecting what matters far more. Yet the Bible tells us that wisdom is more precious than money.

A young man came into a large fortune, and he became proud and arrogant. He traded his money for a luxury car, expensive clothes, and a lavish lifestyle, but he lost his close relationships with his family and friends. He was rich, but he was lonely.

Another man, by contrast, invested in wisdom. He worked hard at learning, read the Bible, and spent time with wise people. Through wisdom he learned how to manage money, how to build healthy relationships, and how to become a person of worth. He did not possess great wealth, but he possessed inner peace and joy.
This story tells us that wisdom is a greater treasure than money. Money can give us material comforts, but wisdom can bring us true abundance and happiness.

In our lives, we need to seek wisdom. By reading Scripture, praying, and talking with wise people, we can grow in wisdom. Wisdom helps us make the right choices, solve problems, and find a way out in hard times. Wisdom makes us better people and influences our families and communities.

So let us stop chasing only money and pursue wisdom instead. Let us invest our time and energy in learning and in developing our wisdom. In this way we will gain more profit, not only materially but, even more, spiritually.
a: Be Convinced of the Value of Wisdom (Proverbs 3

:14 tells us that the value of wisdom far exceeds silver and fine gold. Wisdom helps us make wise choices, avoid mistakes, and move toward success. Wisdom helps us build good relationships and earn the respect and trust of others. Wisdom helps us solve problems, overcome difficulties, and reach our life goals. How to put it into practice: Set your values straight in daily life; do not value only material wealth, but give greater weight to the pursuit of wisdom. Learn from wise people and ask them about their life experience and way of handling things. When you meet difficulty or setbacks, think calmly and seek the guidance of wisdom.

Study Wisdom Diligently. Wisdom is not something we are born with; it must be gained through diligent learning. There are many ways to learn, including reading, thinking, and practice. Build good study habits and steadily accumulate knowledge and experience. How to put it into practice: Set aside time each day to read and learn new things. Think and reflect often, drawing wisdom from life. Take part in learning activities of all kinds to broaden your horizons.
pr:
Dear Lord God, we ask that You give us a heart of wisdom, so that we may understand Your will and walk in the right way.
We ask that You help us study diligently and keep growing in knowledge and experience.
We ask that You lead us to fear You and to do what pleases You.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you bear abundant fruit on your path in pursuit of wisdom, and may you become a person of wisdom and goodness. Amen.

v: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
b: In this verse, God reminds us that wisdom is worth more than gold, and that a wise choice is better than silver. People often seek wealth and material achievement, yet overlook the wisdom that can truly give us an abundant life.

There is a story about a businessman who invested a great deal of money in the pursuit of wealth. He worked with all his heart, disregarding his health and his family. In the end he succeeded financially, but he lost the warmth and happiness of his family. He discovered that money could not solve the emptiness and loneliness inside him.

On the other hand, a young man decided to seek wisdom rather than riches. He spent most of his time reading, studying, and talking with wise people. Although he did not possess much material wealth, he achieved great success in his relationships, his career, and his personal growth. He chose the wise path rather than chasing fleeting money.

This story tells us that pursuing wisdom is more important than wealth. Wisdom gives us guidance and the ability to make wise decisions, and it helps us make the right choices in life. It lets us see the value and meaning of life, and it helps us build deeper relationships with God and with others.

So let us pray to God every day, asking Him to give us wisdom and understanding. Let us pursue not only material success but also richness of soul and spiritual growth. Let us choose wisdom and not be tangled up in the deceptions of the world.
ah: Proverbs 16:16 teaches us, “How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is more desirable than silver.” To put this wise teaching into practice in our lives, we can:
a: Sincerely ask God to give us heavenly wisdom and understanding, more than the riches of the world.
Humbly learn the lessons of wisdom in God’s Word, and let the truth shape our values for life.
Ask spiritual elders for advice, and learn from them the lessons of living a wise life.
Handle money wisely, using it to acquire wisdom, such as by investing in books and in equipping ourselves.
Run our lives with wisdom, pursuing the life goals of glorifying God and serving others.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that Your Word shows us that getting wisdom is better than gold, and that choosing understanding is better than silver. Give us a heart that sincerely seeks wisdom above wealth. Help us wholeheartedly receive the wise teaching of Scripture and let the truth guide our values for life. We also ask that You make us willing to humbly seek advice from elders and learn from their wise lives. Help us use money to acquire wisdom, such as by investing in equipping ourselves. Finally, give us wisdom to run our lives, pursuing the goals of glorifying You and serving others. We pray in the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you seek wisdom in your daily life and build the foundation of your life on wise choices. May your heart be filled with love and hope. Amen.

v: Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
b: In this passage, God reminds us of the value and power of wisdom. Though we often praise bravery and strength, the Bible tells us that wisdom surpasses them all. Wisdom is the ability to make right choices in our lives; it not only helps us deal with difficulties and challenges, but also leads us onto the right path.

Yet this passage also mentions that the poor man’s wisdom is despised and his words are not heard. This reminds us to be humble and to treasure the value of wisdom. Whatever our social position, wisdom is an important resource in our lives. We must not overlook a person’s wisdom just because we cannot see their appearance or wealth.

Let us look at a story. There was a young farmer who had a strong body and great strength. He was always proud of his strength and believed it was enough. But one day he met an old man, small and thin, yet possessing very deep wisdom. The two began to talk, and the old man shared his insights about life and the value of wisdom.

The farmer was amazed. He had never realized that wisdom could surpass the effectiveness of might. He began to appreciate and learn from the old man’s wisdom, and found that wisdom not only helped him manage his farm better, but also guided him in getting along with people and facing challenges.
This story tells us that even if we have great strength or a superior position, wisdom is what we truly need. Wisdom helps us make wise choices in life and leads us onto the right path.

In our lives, we may meet poor people who perhaps have no material abundance or social standing, but who possess precious wisdom. Let us not look down on them, but be willing to listen to their words and experience, and learn and grow from them.
ah: Ecclesiastes 9:16 tells us, “Wisdom is better than might.” To put this wise teaching into practice in our lives, we can:
a: Humbly seek heavenly wisdom from God, rather than relying on might alone and our own cleverness.
Observe the wise people around us, and learn the wise principles by which they handle things.
When facing difficulties, first think through a response with wisdom rather than acting on emotional impulse.
Speak and communicate with wisdom, expressing ourselves appropriately and constructively, and so influence others.
Even in poor circumstances, treasure and practice the lessons of wisdom we have received in life.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, Your Word shows us that wisdom is better than might. Enlighten us, so that we do not act on bravado and our own cleverness alone, but humbly seek the heavenly wisdom that comes from You. Help us observe and learn from the wise people around us and receive their wisdom for living. Give us wisdom, too, to think through ways of responding to life’s many difficulties, and not to act on emotional impulse. Help us communicate with wisdom and fitting words, and have a positive influence. Though our position may be poor, we ask that You help us treasure and practice every lesson of wisdom we have received. We pray in the holy name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be guided by wisdom today and make wise choices. May you treasure the value of wisdom and be willing to learn from those who are overlooked yet possess wisdom. Amen.

v: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
b: When we think about this verse, we see that wisdom is a powerful weapon, more potent than any weapon used in war. At the same time, we should notice that the presence of a sinner can destroy much that is good.

Imagine a country that has the most advanced weapons and military training, but whose leaders lack wisdom and seek only power and greed. As a result, the country is wrapped in chaos and conflict, and its people suffer in the flames of war.

This story reminds us of the importance of wisdom. Wisdom is foresight and insight; it guides us to make right decisions and avoid needless war and destruction. Wisdom enables us to tell right from wrong, to hold firmly to the truth, and to walk the path of justice and fairness.

However, we must also be wary of the influence of a sinner. One sinner’s actions and choices can have a negative effect on those around them. Just as one rotten apple can spoil the whole basket, one sinner’s wrongdoing can spread over many good things, bringing chaos and harm.

So let us ask God to give us wisdom, so that we can be messengers of truth who guide and inspire those around us. Let us stay away from the temptations of sin and live out the hope and love God has given us.
a: Pursue Wisdom (Ecclesiastes 9

:18 tells us that wisdom is better than weapons of war. In this world, many things cannot be solved by force; only wisdom can help us overcome difficulties and succeed. So we should make the pursuit of wisdom our first task. How to put it into practice: Spend time each day reading and meditating on God’s Word, drawing wisdom from God. Learn from wise people and ask about their life experience and way of handling things. Think and reflect often in daily life, and keep accumulating wisdom.
Act Carefully (Ecclesiastes 9

:18 reminds us that one sinner destroys much good. However much wisdom we have, we still need to act carefully and avoid falling into the traps of sinners. In dealing with others, be on guard and do not trust people too easily. Before making important decisions, think carefully and ask for God’s guidance. How to put it into practice: Do not keep company with wicked people, lest you be influenced by them. Be careful in your words and actions to avoid offending others. When you meet difficulty or temptation, seek God’s help and rely on His strength.

Do Good with Wisdom. Wisdom is not only for obtaining success; it must also be used to do good and help others. Only when wisdom is used for good deeds does its true value show. We should take an active part in public-service activities and use our wisdom and strength to help those in need. How to put it into practice: Care about the people around you and take the initiative to lend a hand. Take part actively in your church’s ministry, serving others with love and wisdom. Share your knowledge and skills with others to help them grow.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, we ask that You give us a heart of wisdom, so that we may understand Your will and walk in the right way.
We ask that You help us act carefully, stay far from evil, and live lives that glorify You.
We ask that You give us the strength to do good with wisdom, so that we can help others with love and wisdom.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you act in wisdom, and may your words and deeds bring others faith, hope, and love. Amen.

v: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
b: In this passage, God reminds us of the value of wisdom. Wisdom is a precious resource that guides us to make the right choices and keeps us from walking into the way of folly and darkness. Just as light overcomes darkness, wisdom overcomes folly.

Everyone comes to times of choosing, and sometimes we may get lost in confusion and bewilderment. But when we seek wisdom and guidance, God will surely show us the right way. He gives wisdom so that we can see the truth of things and avoid making wrong decisions.

A young man stood at a crossroads with two roads before him. One was a wide, bright highway; the other was a narrow, dim path. Confused about which to choose, the young man decided to pray to God and ask for wisdom and guidance.

In prayer, because of his faith in God and his longing for Him, the light of wisdom shone into his heart. He understood that the wide highway represented worldly temptation and pleasure, while the narrow path symbolized loyalty, integrity, and devotion. In the end he chose the narrow path, and was willing to stand firm for his faith and values.

This story reminds us that when we face choices, wisdom is our best companion. When we long to understand God’s will, He will surely give us wisdom. Wisdom helps us tell right from wrong, so that we can make the right decisions.

So let us seek wisdom every day, through reading the Bible, praying, and talking with wise people, so that we can walk the path of light in our lives. When we apply wisdom to our daily decisions, we will find that God’s blessing and guidance are always with us.
a: Pursue Wisdom (Ecclesiastes 2

:13 tells us that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness. Wisdom helps us see the truth of things, make right choices, and avoid mistakes. Folly leaves us lost in confusion, making wrong choices and heading toward failure. How to put it into practice: Spend time each day reading and meditating on God’s Word, drawing wisdom from God. Learn from wise people and ask about their life experience and way of handling things. Think and reflect often in daily life, and keep accumulating wisdom.
Cast Off Folly (Ecclesiastes 2

:13 reminds us that folly is like darkness: it blinds our eyes so that we cannot see the truth of things. So we should do our best to cast off folly and let the light of wisdom shine into our hearts. How to put it into practice: Do not be deceived by worldly values; hold to the truth and pursue righteousness. Do not indulge in pleasure; keep a clear head and think and act rationally. Do not trust others too easily; learn to think independently and tell right from wrong.

Live with Wisdom. Wisdom must not only be understood, but practiced. We should apply wisdom to every area of daily life, make wise choices, and live a meaningful life. How to put it into practice: In study, have a right attitude, be diligent and hardworking, and pursue knowledge and truth. In work, be responsible and conscientious, and create value. In life, treat people sincerely, be glad to help others, and spread love.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, we ask that You give us a heart of wisdom, so that we may understand Your will and walk in the right way.
We ask that You help us cast off folly, and let the light of wisdom shine into our hearts.
We ask that You give us the strength to live with wisdom, so that we may live lives that glorify You.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive wisdom from God every day, so that you can stay far from the temptations of folly and darkness and walk in the path of light. Amen.

v: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
b: In this verse, God reminds us to become wise people. Many times we face difficulties, challenges, and mockery, but if we have wisdom, we can respond to these situations with the right attitude and actions.

Imagine a little child learning to ride a bicycle. At first he may fall, but he is not discouraged. Instead he learns how to keep his balance, how to turn, and how to push the pedals. He learns from every failure and keeps working at it, and in the end he succeeds in riding the bicycle.

This story tells us that wisdom is not only knowledge and understanding; it also includes adaptability and a spirit of perseverance. When we meet difficulties, we can learn from our mistakes and find ways to solve the problem.

In the same way, the Christian life needs wisdom. We may face temptation, hardship, and the world’s ridicule. But if we hold fast to God’s truth and respond with a wise heart, we will be able to get out of our difficulties and become His witnesses.

Let us improve ourselves every day, learning wisdom under the teaching of the Bible, and treating others with love and humility in daily life. When we become wise people, we will not only feel God’s delight, but also be able to answer those who mock us.
ah: Proverbs 27:11 urges us to be wise people, to make God’s heart glad and to be able to answer those who reproach us. To become wise people, in daily life we can:
a: Humbly read the Bible and receive God’s wise teaching, letting the truth guide how we live.
Pray often to seek God’s guidance and wisdom, and ask for His will when making major decisions.
Observe and learn from people around us who have wise character, and draw life wisdom from them.
Manage time, money, and resources with wisdom, making wise arrangements in order of importance.
Discern right from wrong with wisdom, stay away from the influence of folly, and live out a witness consistent with biblical wisdom.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, Your Word commands us to be wise people. Help us humbly receive the wise teaching of Scripture, and let the truth guide how we live and act. Give us the wisdom to pray often and seek Your will, and to ask for Your guidance when we face major decisions in life. Help us observe and learn from the people around us who have wise character, and draw precious life experience and wisdom from them. Give us wisdom, too, to manage what we have been given, making wise arrangements in order of importance. Finally, give us wisdom to discern right from wrong, to stay away from the influence of worldly folly, and to live out a wise witness to the Lord, so that Your heart is glad and delighted. We pray in the holy name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you grow into a wise person each day, and face the challenges and trials of life with love and hope. Amen.

v: Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise,
b: In these brief but deeply meaningful words, we are invited to reflect on our conduct and our choices. In our daily lives, every day is full of opportunities to choose, and these choices shape who we are and who we will become.

Let us think about the true meaning of wisdom. Wisdom is not merely a display of knowledge or intellect, but the right use of knowledge. Wisdom is the ability to make the best choice in a difficult situation; it is the art of knowing when to speak and when to keep silent. Here God teaches us that wise conduct is far better than foolish impulse.

A young rock climber faces a difficult stretch of the mountain he has never tried before. If he impulsively chooses a route that looks fast but is dangerous, it could bring unforeseen consequences. But if he stops, assesses the situation, and asks the advice of experienced climbers, he may choose a safer route that may take longer. This is wisdom in action: not only for the moment, but for long-term safety and success.

In our lives, each of us faces similar choices. When we are under pressure at work, feel tension in family relationships, or are unsure about a personal decision, this verse reminds us to act carefully and choose the way of wisdom. That may mean seeking a mentor’s advice, taking time to pray and meditate, or simply considering every important decision from a long-term perspective.

So as we leave here today and set out on our separate roads, let us carry with us a longing for wisdom. When we face decisions, let us choose actions that reflect our commitment to truth, love, and justice.
a: Self-Examination and Honesty
In your daily conduct, always keep watch over yourself, making sure every decision is well thought through. When you face difficulty or temptation, choose the path of honesty and integrity.
Put Others First
In making decisions, consider the effect of your actions on others. Wise people seek win-win solutions and actively build positive relationships.
Regular Self-Assessment
Each week, take time to reflect on the past week’s conduct, and assess which actions were wise and which need improvement. This will help you keep growing and improve the quality of your decisions.
Keep Learning and Growing
Keep learning through reading, listening to lectures, or taking part in workshops. Wisdom comes not only from accumulating knowledge, but also from applying and practicing it.
Seek Spiritual Guidance
Seek spiritual guidance in life and work. Prayer and meditation on the Bible can help you keep a clear and peaceful heart when facing decisions.
pr: Dear Lord, we ask that You give us wisdom, so that in our conduct every day we may reflect Your image. Help us walk carefully in daily life, not imitating the unwise but becoming wise people. Lead us to consider others in all our decisions, and to keep assessing ourselves and learning, so that our conduct may bring more glory to You. Give us spiritual insight, so that we may be light and salt in this world. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God give you a wise heart, to discern right from wrong and choose the best path, and may He fill your life with love, hope, and faith. Amen!

v: Whoever keeps the law is a wise son; but he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father.
b: In this saying, we can see a choice between two paths: one is the path of wisdom and dignity, the other is the path of indulgence and shame. This is not only guidance for our daily conduct, but a deep insight into the choices we make in life.

There was a young man who faced many temptations and challenges as he grew up. In his community, many young people chose the easy road: pursuing quick success, even if it meant sacrificing morals and values. But this young man chose a different path. He kept at his studies, respected his family, and held to his faith. These choices were not easy, and often meant giving up short-term pleasure. But over time he not only won the respect of the community, he also built his own business and became a respected leader.

This story shows us the true meaning of “Whoever keeps the law is a wise son.” When we choose to follow God’s law, even when the world around us tempts us in the opposite direction, we gain deeper peace and satisfaction. Wisdom is not just the accumulation of knowledge, but our ability to apply that knowledge to make right decisions.

In contrast, “he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father” reminds us that our choices and conduct affect not only ourselves but also those we love. When we choose to associate with people who pursue short-term pleasure and ignore long-term consequences, we not only move away from the path of wisdom, but may also bring shame on our families.

So as we walk out of here today and face the many choices of life, let us remember the teaching of this verse. Choose the path of the wise son, and stay away from behavior that could bring shame to us and our families. Let our lives bring honor to our parents and to our Heavenly Father.
a: **Keep the Law and Principles**
In life, hold firmly to God’s teaching and to the laws of society. This includes not only obeying the laws of the land but also our moral and ethical standards.
**Choose Good Companions**
Avoid close association with people who might lure us off the right path. Choose friends who will encourage you and grow with you.
**Honor Your Family**
Through your conduct, make your family proud and do not bring them shame. This means considering the effect on your family in every decision.
**Self-Reflection and Responsibility**
Regularly examine your conduct and motives, make sure they meet spiritual and moral standards, and take responsibility for your actions.
**Flee Temptation**
Identify the temptations in your life that might lead you off the right path, and actively look for ways to avoid them.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for today’s teaching, reminding us to be wise sons and to keep Your law. Give us strength and wisdom to choose the right friends and to avoid temptations that might turn us from Your way. Help us honor our families through our conduct, and testify to Your glory with our lives. May we always examine ourselves, take responsibility for our actions, and stand firm in Your love. We pray in the holy name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you show the bearing of a wise son at every step of life, so that your conduct becomes proof of your faith and brings honor and dignity to you and those you love. Amen!

v: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during the harvest is a son who causes shame.
b: This passage reminds us that wisdom concerns not only our conduct but also how we manage and use our time. A wise son knows how to seize the moment; when opportunity comes, he is ready and acts. But those who choose to rest or delay at the critical moment end up ashamed, because they have lost a precious opportunity.

Let us look at a practical example of how this principle applies in our lives. Imagine a farmer and his two children. In the hot summer, when the crops are ripe, one child gets up early every day, unafraid of the heat, and works hard to make sure every ripe fruit is harvested in time. The other chooses to rest in the cool of the house and often misses the best time for harvest. When the harvest season ends, the first child’s storehouse is full of produce, while the second child is ashamed of his laziness and neglect.

This story reflects the realities of farming, but it also symbolizes many scenes in our lives. When we have the chance to act in our studies, our careers, or our relationships, do we choose to throw ourselves into it, or do we shrink back and hope things will resolve themselves? A wise son chooses the former, because he knows that true achievement and fulfillment come only through active effort and timely action.

Today, let each of us ask ourselves: Am I actively preparing and harvesting, or am I choosing to rest at the critical moment? Our choices will decide whether we become wise sons, or feel ashamed for having missed our chance.
a: **Work Diligently**

Use the present opportunity to work diligently, like the wise son who gathers in summer. Do not slack off or delay when you should be working; look for every opportunity to improve and take an active part.
**Plan for the Future**

Just as a farmer plans ahead for harvest, we too should set goals and make plans for the future. This includes short-term and long-term goals, so that you have a clear direction and are prepared for what lies ahead.
**Avoid Laziness**

Be alert to any form of laziness or procrastination. Develop the habit of checking your progress and goals each day, which will help you keep your motivation and make sure you are ready in the harvest season.
**Manage Your Time**
Manage your time effectively, making sure you do important work in your most productive hours. Use tools and techniques to improve how you use time, such as time-blocking or to-do lists.
**Seek Wisdom**
Regularly seek God’s wisdom and guidance, and through prayer and Bible reading strengthen your sensitivity to when to act. This will help you make wise choices at the right time.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word how to be wise sons. Give us a diligent and farsighted heart, so that we can gather at the right time and avoid sleeping through the harvest. Help us manage our time effectively, avoid laziness and procrastination, and always seek wisdom and guidance from You. May our conduct glorify You, and through our diligence may we show our love and faithfulness to You. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be a wise son in every season, seizing every opportunity and reaping a full harvest. May your actions and decisions bring you honor rather than shame. Amen!

v: The LORD’s Spirit will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.
b: This passage describes a person filled by God, one who has wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord. It is an extremely comprehensive picture of the spiritual life, teaching us how to be open to God at every level and let His Spirit lead our lives.

Think of an outstanding architect who has designed many award-winning buildings. His success lies not only in his learning, but in how he turns that knowledge into innovative designs, which takes wisdom and understanding. He must understand the nature of materials, consider structural stability, and create spaces that are both beautiful and useful. In addition, his passion for his work and his reverence for architecture drive him to keep pursuing excellence.

This is exactly the message today’s verse wants to convey: when the Spirit of the Lord is among us, He gives us not only the ability to act, but also wisdom and knowledge beyond the ordinary, so that we can do better in every way. This applies not only to architects but to every one of us in our careers and daily lives. Whether we are teachers, doctors, parents, or students, God’s Spirit can inspire us in our work and relationships.

This change from the inside out is real. When we let the Spirit of the Lord dwell in our hearts, we begin to make wiser decisions, to look at the world around us with more compassion, and to face challenges more strongly. Our reverence for God not only makes us humble, but also helps us stay calm and steady in the storms of life.
a: **Seek the Filling of the Holy Spirit**
Every day, through prayer, ask the Holy Spirit to fill you and give you wisdom and understanding, so that God’s wisdom shows in your daily decisions.
**Cultivate Counsel and Might**
In work and daily life, actively look for opportunities to improve your strategic thinking and practical skills, such as taking training courses or accepting new challenges.
**Grow in Knowledge**
Regularly invest time in learning new knowledge and skills, whether through reading, online courses, or discussion with others, and let knowledge be the cornerstone of your wisdom.
**Deepen the Fear of the Lord**
Make the fear of the Lord the core of your life, and cultivate it through daily devotions, prayer, and taking part in church activities.
**Apply What You Learn to Show Wisdom**
When facing challenges and decisions in life, apply the wisdom you have learned from the Bible, show your understanding and counsel, and use it to solve problems and lead others.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for giving us wisdom and understanding through Your Spirit. Lead us in every step of our daily lives, so that under the guidance of Your Spirit we make wise decisions. Give us counsel and might, so that we can act effectively and grow in knowledge as we learn. Help us deepen our reverence for You, and let that reverence guide every action and decision. Make us witnesses of wisdom, glorifying Your name. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your life, under the guidance of God’s Spirit, be filled with wisdom, understanding, counsel, and might, so that in all you do you show forth God’s glory. May you feel knowledge and the fear of God at every step, making each of your days more meaningful and fulfilling. Amen!

v: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
b: This passage reminds us that every day is precious, and teaches us how to treasure time and fill it with meaning. To number our days means to think carefully about how we live and the decisions we make, and so to cultivate a heart of wisdom.

An old carpenter was about to retire, and he decided to make one last piece, which would sum up the skills of his whole life. He spent a great deal of time planning, choosing each material with care and making every part with attention. He knew his time was limited, and every day had to count. When it was finished, the piece not only showed his craftsmanship, but also reflected his thoughtfulness and wisdom about life. This is the practice of numbering our days: let every moment count, and turn it into wisdom.

In our lives, this wisdom of numbering our days can be seen in many ways. A teacher, for example, carefully prepares every lesson to make sure her students learn not only knowledge, but also how to use that knowledge to solve problems. Or a doctor listens attentively to each patient’s needs and provides care in the wisest way.

Through these examples, we see that when we ask God to teach us how to number our days, we become not only more efficient in managing time, but our hearts also grow more mature, and our way of treating life becomes more compassionate and understanding.
a: **Learn to Treasure Time**

Be aware that life is limited; wake up each day with gratitude and treasure every minute and second of the present. Use a schedule or journal to track how you use your time, making sure each day is meaningful.
**Set Life Goals**
Set clear short-term and long-term goals to help you focus on what matters. These goals should reflect your personal values and your hopes for life.
**Practice Self-Reflection**
At the end of each day, take time to reflect on your conduct and what you learned, assessing what was effective and what needs to be improved. This helps you keep growing and increase your wisdom.
**Learn New Things**
Keep learning new knowledge and skills, whether through books, lectures, or conversations with others. This continued learning can broaden your horizons and enrich your experience.
**Cultivate a Thankful Heart**

Spend time each day giving thanks for the good things and experiences in your life. This will not only increase your happiness, but also develop a heart of wisdom that better understands the meaning and value of life.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for giving us each day of life. We ask that You teach us how to number our days, so that we can realize how precious time is and live a purposeful, meaningful life under Your guidance. Help us set and achieve life goals, reflect helpfully on ourselves, and keep learning and growing. Give us thankful hearts, so that in every day we can see Your grace and guidance. We ask that You make our hearts wiser, so that we can use each moment wisely and glorify Your name. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God give you the wisdom to number your days, so that each of your days is full of meaning and your soul keeps growing and being enriched. May your life be measured not only in days, but reflect eternal value. Amen!

v: Whoever keeps the commandment shall not come to harm, and his wise heart will know the time and procedure.
b: This passage reminds us that wisdom is not only the accumulation of knowledge, but the ability to understand and adapt to all kinds of situations in life. A wise person knows how to make the right decision at the right time, because his heart discerns time and judgment.

An entrepreneur decided to start a business in a time of economic uncertainty. Many thought it was a very risky decision, but he not only studied the market carefully, but also understood consumers’ needs and industry trends. His wisdom came not only from his analysis of the data, but from knowing when to act. As a result, his company not only survived the hard times, but eventually flourished.

This story shows how wise people use their understanding of time and judgment to avoid disaster and seize opportunity. The use of wisdom applies not only to business decisions but equally to our personal lives: how we manage our health, our relationships, and our personal growth.

Wisdom also means understanding the rhythm of life and its natural laws. These are not only the laws of the material world, but also spiritual and moral norms. When we keep God’s commandments, our lives will be more harmonious, because we are in line with the God who created us.
So let us seek God’s wisdom, and learn how to discern the time and follow divine principles. This will not only help us avoid needless hardship, but fill our journey through life with peace and joy.
a: **Faithfully Keep God’s Commandments**
In daily life, strive to follow the teaching of the Bible. This includes not only obvious rules of conduct, but also an attitude of love, tolerance, and integrity.
**Learn to Recognize the Right Time**

Wise people can discern what action is needed in different situations. Try to learn to read the needs of a situation, which may come through observation, learning from the experience of others, or actively listening to the opinions and advice of those around you.
**Understand and Practice Principles**

Gain a deep understanding and application of the patterns and principles you meet in life. This can come through learning concrete life skills, such as time management and financial planning, so that you can better steer the course of your life.
**Develop Decision-Making Ability**

Improve the quality of your decisions through practice in actual decision-making. Set up scenarios and simulate the consequences of decisions, so that you can learn and grow without real consequences.
**Continual Self-Reflection**

Reflect regularly on yourself and assess whether your decisions meet the standard of wise people’s conduct. You can do this through journaling, sharing your reflections, or discussion with trusted friends and mentors.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word how to be wise people. Give us the wisdom to recognize the right time and the right principles, so that we may walk in keeping Your commandments. Help us keep learning and practicing in daily life, improve our decision-making, and grow through continual self-reflection. May our lives and decisions reflect Your wisdom and grace. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your heart be full of wisdom, discerning every moment and following every divine principle. As you walk, may you be spared all evil and experience boundless blessing and peace. Amen!

v: The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.
b: This passage reveals the deep connection between wisdom and speech. A truly wise person is clear not only in thought but also very careful in expression. His words convey not only information, but wisdom and knowledge.

Imagine a teacher who not only imparts knowledge in the classroom, but also sets an example for his students by his words and actions in life. He knows well that every sentence and every conversation is a chance to shape a young mind. As in the verse we have read, his heart directs his speech, so that his teaching is full of wisdom and inspiration. What his students learn from him is not only what is in books, but how to think and how to live.

The power of this wisdom is not limited to education. In the family, parents’ words can encourage and shape their children’s future. In the workplace, a leader’s way of communicating can affect the morale and efficiency of the team. Among friends, our conversation can be constructive or destructive. Wise people always choose the former, because their hearts have trained their mouths to be a source of knowledge and positive influence.
When our hearts are full of wisdom, our words will naturally be full of grace. This is a powerful truth, and if we follow it, it can change how we interact with others, and even change our lives.
a: **Cultivate Wisdom of Mind**
In daily life, keep enriching and deepening your mind through reading, study, and thinking. This will naturally be reflected in your language and conversation.
**Think Before You Speak**
Before speaking, take time to consider how your words can be more constructive and instructive. This not only helps avoid needless misunderstanding, but also improves communication.
**Listen to Others**
Increase your learning by listening to others’ insights and knowledge. This will not only widen your horizons, but also deepen your understanding and compassion.
**Choose Your Words Carefully**
In conversation, choose the right words and tone to make dialogue more inspiring and encouraging. This makes communication more effective and strengthens the influence of your words.
**Reflect and Apply What You Learn**
Apply the knowledge you gain from books, conversations, and experience to daily life. This not only promotes your own growth but also helps those around you learn from your words and deeds.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for teaching us wisdom through Your Word. Give us wise hearts that instruct our mouths, so that our lips may add to learning. Help us think, listen, and choose our words carefully in our conversations every day, so that our words become bridges for others to learn. Help us apply all we have learned in daily life, so that we may better serve You and those around us. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your heart be full of wisdom, so that your words become a light in other people’s lives, guiding them on their way and bringing knowledge and encouragement. May your words always reflect the wisdom and love in your heart. Amen!

v: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
b: This passage reminds us that a wise heart knows how to seek growth in hardship, rather than merely pursuing surface happiness. Wise people know that the challenges and sorrows of life are opportunities for deep learning and growth.

A young man had just lost his dear father. It was a severe blow, but he chose to turn that grief into strength to move him forward. He began working harder, took an active part in community activities, and devoted himself to helping others who had gone through similar pain. Through his pain he learned empathy, resilience, and how to influence the lives of others. His experience proves that even in “the house of mourning,” we can find strength and wisdom.

This stands in sharp contrast to fools, who may choose to escape reality, immersing themselves in fleeting pleasure and avoidance, and ignoring chances to grow. Such a way of life may feel happy for a while, but in the end it cannot bring true inner satisfaction or deep personal growth.

So when we face the low points of life, we should be like the wise and look for opportunities to learn and grow from them, rather than escaping reality and seeking momentary comfort. This wisdom lets us stand stronger in adversity and draw lessons from every experience, enriching our lives.
a: **Cultivate Compassion and Understanding**
When others meet with grief or hardship, show understanding and compassion. When others experience loss, offer support and comfort rather than avoiding them or ignoring their feelings.
**Face Reality**

Learn to face the unavoidable difficulties and sorrows of life, rather than running from them or immersing yourself in false happiness. This helps cultivate a deeper experience of life and a truer knowledge of yourself.
**Learn to Grow Through Pain**
See the challenges and difficulties you meet as opportunities for growth and learning. Look for the lessons in them and let them lift you spiritually and emotionally.
**Take Part in Community Support**
Take an active part in community support and comfort activities, such as joining a bereavement group or volunteering, helping others while also enriching your own experience.
**Value Deep Relationships**
In your interactions, seek deep and meaningful connection, not just surface happiness and entertainment. This helps build more lasting and valuable relationships.
pr: Dear Lord, we ask that You give us wisdom, so that our hearts may find meaning and value in life’s difficulties and sorrows. Help us offer support and comfort in the house of mourning, learn and grow from it, and take an active part in helping others. Make our relationships deeper and more meaningful, and let us show Your love and compassion each day. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. When you face the pain of life, may your heart find wisdom and strength, turning every challenge into a chance for growth and progress. May your life be not only a search for happiness, but a pursuit of meaning and depth. Amen!

v: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
b: This passage teaches us that the power of words is immense: they can wound, and they can heal. Wise people know how to use this power to bring positive influence rather than negative harm.

A school teacher noticed that a student, normally introverted and lacking in confidence, had recently become even more downcast. One day she decided to use her words to encourage him, telling him she saw his potential and believed he could do better. Those words were like gentle spring rain: they not only lifted the student’s confidence, but changed his attitude toward learning. From then on, the student’s grades and social skills improved markedly.

This story proves the truth of “the tongue of the wise heals.” Positive, encouraging words can heal the soul and give people strength and confidence. Conversely, rash and negative words are like sharp blades that can cause deep wounds.

Using words wisely is not just saying nice things; it is saying the right thing at the right time. In our daily lives, whether at home, at work, or in social settings, we should learn how to use our words effectively, to build up rather than tear down, and to encourage rather than discourage.
a: **Choose Your Words Carefully**
Think before you speak, and choose words that encourage and build up others, avoiding rash and hurtful language.
**Learn Effective Communication**
Develop good listening skills and empathy, so that conversation becomes a tool for understanding and solving problems rather than for arguing or hurting.
**Practice Positive Feedback**
Offer constructive feedback rather than criticism, helping others grow and improve, so that your words become a help to their progress.
**Encourage and Motivate Others**
Use your words to motivate and inspire others, especially when they face challenges or difficulties, and become a source of strength for them.
**Reflect on and Correct Your Own Speech**
Regularly reflect on your language and way of communicating, and make necessary adjustments to make sure you always communicate with others in wisdom and love.
pr: Dear Lord, we ask that You give us wisdom, so that our tongues may become healing medicine for others. Help us show Your love and compassion in our words, and avoid any rash or hurtful speech. Give us empathy and wisdom, so that we can talk with others in constructive and encouraging ways. Let our words not only express thoughts, but also carry care and support. We ask that You guide every word we speak, so that it becomes a witness to Your love. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your words become healing medicine to those around you. May your tongue bring hope and comfort, so that everyone who hears your voice feels love and care. Amen!

v: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouths of fools gush out folly.
b: In this verse, we see the contrast between wisdom and folly. The wise use their tongues to speak words of knowledge; they express themselves with intelligence and care, and their words can inspire hearts and give people hope and love. By contrast, the mouth of a fool pours out only foolish words; they lack insight and good sense, and their words may cause harm and misunderstanding.

In our lives, are we wise people? Are our tongues used to convey knowledge and wisdom? Or do we often speak meaningless words offhandedly, even hurting others? Let us put away the tongue of a fool and begin to learn how to become a wise person.
