We can find inspiration in a story. There was once a wise old man who was famous in his village. When people came to him for advice and wisdom, he always answered them with insightful words. One day a young man came before him and asked, “I often cannot control my tongue. How can I become a wise person?” The old man heard the question, smiled, and answered, “My child, you must learn to stop and think before you speak. Ask yourself, is this worth saying? Will it bring benefit to others? If not, then keep silent.”

This story tells us that becoming a wise person requires us to learn self-control and caution. When we face strong emotion or confusion, we must learn to pause and think, and let the knowledge we have gained from the Word guide our speech. Do not speak words casually, but choose words that will bring benefit to people.

So in our daily lives, let us use the tongue of the wise to express our knowledge and wisdom. Let us use our words to encourage, inspire, and love others. When we learn to govern our tongues, we will become instruments God is willing to use, bringing more faith, hope, and love to this world.
a: **Deepen Knowledge and Understanding**
Keep learning new knowledge and deepen your understanding of what you already know, so that when you open your mouth, you will naturally share information of depth and value.
**Think Carefully Before Speaking**
Before giving an opinion, take time to consider the effect of your words. Make sure what you say helps the situation, and give information or opinions in a constructive way.
**Improve Communication Skills**
Learn to express your thoughts effectively, including choice of words, adjusting your tone, and conveying emotion, so that your communication is both clear and influential.
**Practice Patience and Empathy**
Show patience and empathy when you talk with people. This will help you better understand the other person’s needs and respond more appropriately.
**Influence Others Positively**
Strive to make your words a positive influence on others. Whether through encouragement, guidance, or providing knowledge, let your words help others along the road of growth.
pr: Dear Lord, we ask that You give us wisdom, so that our tongues may use knowledge rightly. Help us show Your wisdom and love in what we say, and avoid foolish words. Let our communication not only convey information but express care and understanding. Give us the ability to use knowledge in our conversations, so that we may influence others in constructive and encouraging ways. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be a wise person, using your tongue to speak words of knowledge, and bringing others faith, hope, and love. Amen.

v: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
b: This passage deeply reminds us that our words have the power both to build up and to tear down. The words of the wise are full of grace, able to encourage and lift those who hear them, while thoughtless words can lead to self-destruction.

A community leader was respected because he often treated others with encouraging and positive words. At one community meeting, he faced great opposition and criticism. Yet he chose not to respond with anger, but explained his views and plans with kindness and understanding. This attitude not only calmed the tension in the room, but strengthened trust and respect among the members of the community.

On the other hand, we have also seen examples where impulsive or thoughtless speech has caused needless consequences. For example, a business manager, in a moment of anger and careless words, not only hurt an employee’s feelings but also weakened the team’s morale. This is how a fool’s words swallow up a person’s authority and influence.

These examples teach us that words are a powerful tool. Wise people know that every sentence is an opportunity to nurture a relationship, build trust, or offer support. Every conversation is a chance to shape the world around us.

So as we talk each day with family, friends, and colleagues, let us choose words that bring a positive effect. Let our words be gracious words, like gentle rain that refreshes the heart, rather than poison that harms the soul.
a: **Speak Gracious Words**
In everyday conversation, let every word be full of grace and encouragement. Avoid sharp or hurtful language, and choose words that build people up and offer support and motivation.
**Reflect on the Effect of Your Words**
Before you speak, think about how your words will affect others. Try to listen to your own words from the other person’s point of view, and make sure your language brings a positive effect.
**Train Yourself to Listen Well**
Be a good listener, so that you can better understand the other person’s needs and feelings, and respond accordingly with the most fitting words.
**Keep Learning and Growing**
Through reading, attending lectures, or group study, improve your communication skills and your ability to handle relationships. Learn how to use words effectively to express love and respect.
**Practice Kindness in Daily Life**
Apply gracious words in all your relationships, whether family, friends, or the workplace. Through your words, let the people around you feel respect and worth.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for teaching us to use gracious words to express Your love and wisdom. We ask that You help us control our tongues, so that our mouths can speak words that build up, avoiding any speech that could cause destruction. Give us wisdom, so that our daily conversations always reflect Your lovingkindness and grace. Help us become effective communicators, encouraging and motivating others with our words. In the name of Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your words always be full of wisdom and grace, a blessing in other people’s lives, and may your words become a source of healing and encouragement. Amen!

v: The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so with the heart of fools.
b: This passage emphasizes how wise people use their words to spread knowledge and truth, while fools fail to do so. The words of the wise not only provide information, but inspire thought and lead their listeners toward good.

A scientist made a major breakthrough in research on renewable energy. But she realized that producing results in the lab was not enough. So she began speaking at conferences and community gatherings, using her wise lips to spread this new knowledge to the public. Her words inspired many young scholars and entrepreneurs to devote themselves to developing environmental technology, and the whole community benefited.

On the other hand, a fool may have the same resources and platform, but for lack of careful thought and respect for knowledge, what he says may mislead or confuse. This wastes the opportunity of having influence, and may also have a negative effect on society.

This tells us that wisdom lies not only in having knowledge, but in how we use it to influence and improve the lives of others. The lips of the wise show their sense of responsibility for that knowledge, and they choose to share it in constructive and positive ways.

So in our daily conversations, we should choose our words as we would choose precious seeds, scattering them on fertile soil and letting the seeds of knowledge take root and sprout in the hearts of our listeners.
a: **Actively Learn and Share Knowledge**
Think of yourself as a lifelong learner, constantly taking in new knowledge. Then find opportunities to share that knowledge in conversation, enriching not only yourself but others.
**Choose Helpful Topics**
In conversation, choose topics that stimulate thought and discussion, and avoid superficial chatter or unconstructive gossip.
**Improve Communication Skills**
Learn to convey information more effectively, including clear expression, good questioning, and effective listening, so that information is accurately sent and received.
**Encourage and Inspire with Words**
Let your words be a help to others’ growth, whether through positive encouragement, constructive feedback, or sharing practical knowledge and experience.
**Be a Thinker and Problem-Solver**
In daily life, show how you solve problems with wisdom, and pass this way of thinking on to others through your words.
pr: Dear Lord, we ask that You give us wisdom, so that our lips can spread knowledge and reflect Your teaching and wisdom in our daily conversations. Help us choose helpful topics, improve our communication skills, and use our words to encourage and inspire others. Make us thinkers who can solve problems, showing Your love and wisdom through our words and actions. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your lips be a fountain of wisdom, and your words an instrument for spreading knowledge and righteousness. May you show your understanding and insight in your speech, so that every word you speak brings light and progress to the world. Amen!

v: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
b: This passage shows us the beautiful connection between discernment and wisdom. The heart of the discerning naturally longs to take in knowledge, while the wise actively seek opportunities to learn. The combination of the two is the foundation of our continued growth and progress.

A young entrepreneur started a technology company. But he soon realized that for the company to keep succeeding, he needed to keep learning about new market trends and technological innovations. So he not only attended industry conferences, but actively sought advice from more experienced entrepreneurs. This attitude of seeking knowledge not only enriched his own store of knowledge, but also helped his company adapt to a rapidly changing market.

This story tells us that whatever our age or occupation, we can keep growing in wisdom through an open mind and ears willing to learn. The pursuit of wisdom is not a sprint but a marathon, requiring continued effort and dedication.

In life, every conversation, every book, and even every failure is a chance to learn. When we open our hearts and listen to the voices around us, our knowledge and understanding will keep expanding. This wisdom not only helps us solve personal and professional problems, but lets us face the many challenges of life with greater composure.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your heart and senses always be open to the light of God’s wisdom. May you keep progressing on your journey of seeking knowledge, and use the knowledge you gain to enrich your own life and the lives of those around you. May your ears always long to hear the voice of truth, and may your heart rejoice as wisdom grows. Amen!

v: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness—and yet I perceived that one event happens to them all.
b: This passage tells us that wise people can see the true nature of things clearly, while fools lose their way in the dark. Yet both the wise and the foolish meet the same difficulties and challenges. This is an unavoidable part of life; everyone faces all kinds of trials and hardships.

It is like a traveler walking along a dark path. He may not know whether there are traps or obstacles ahead. But if he carries a bright lamp in his hand, he can see the path in front of him clearly and avoid danger.

So it is in life: wisdom is like a bright lamp that lights the road ahead of us. When we look at things with the eyes of wisdom, we can understand the meaning and purpose of life. We can tell right from wrong and choose the right road. Wisdom enables us to find light in the darkness and walk out of our difficulties.

Some may think wisdom is an innate gift, but in fact wisdom can be cultivated through learning, observation, and reflection. As a wise man in the Bible says, “Consider the path of your feet, and let all your ways be guided by wisdom” (Proverbs 4:26). By constantly learning and staying aware, we can keep growing in the ability of wisdom.

Let us consider: in our daily lives, do we always hurry to make decisions without taking time to think and consider the consequences? It is time to stop, look at things with the eyes of wisdom, and handle every challenge with calm and reason.
a: **Cultivate Foresight**
Strive to foresee future possibilities and challenges, and prepare for them, so that we can stay steady and forward-looking in uncertain times.
**Stay Aware**
In daily life, stay sensitive and aware of your surroundings. This can help us avoid possible risks and seize opportunities.
**Pursue Spiritual Insight**
Deepen our understanding of life and spiritual truth through prayer, meditation, and study of the Bible, which will make our eyes brighter.
**Learn and Adapt**
When making decisions, use all available resources to increase our knowledge and understanding, so that we can act more wisely.
**Share Wisdom**
Share your insights and experience with others, especially those who may be in difficulty, to help them also see the light that is possible.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for giving us bright eyes, so that we can see truth and hope in this world. We ask that You help us cultivate foresight and stay aware, so that we can avoid the road of darkness. Give us spiritual insight, so that we are full of wisdom in all our decisions. Help us learn, adapt, and gladly share our wisdom, so that we and those around us may benefit. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you look at the small details of life with the eyes of wisdom and understand the meaning and purpose of life. May you keep faith and hope in difficulty, and face every person and every situation with love. May the Lord’s blessing and peace always be with you. Amen.

v: The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn from the snares of death.
b: This passage reminds us that wisdom is not only the accumulation of knowledge; it is an art of living, a way to protect us from danger and guide us toward abundant life. The teaching of wisdom is our refuge, a firm pillar we can rely on in hard times.

An experienced mountain climber faced rugged mountain paths and a sudden blizzard. His survival depended not only on his physical strength, but on his understanding and application of mountaineering wisdom: knowing when to press forward and when to look for shelter. These principles, these guides of wisdom, became a spring of life that delivered him from danger and preserved his life, so that he could return home safely.

In the same way, in our daily lives the teaching of wisdom guides us in making wise choices. Whether we are dealing with the complexity of relationships, facing challenges of professional ethics, or managing our finances, wisdom is our guiding lighthouse.

To be more specific, think of a parent teaching a child to cross the road safely. The rules this parent gives, look left, look right, and check again that no vehicles are coming before crossing, are simple but important lessons of wisdom that give the child a way to avoid danger and become a safety net in their life.
a: **Keep Spiritual Principles**
Make the teaching of the Bible the guide for your life, practicing spiritual principles such as love, forgiveness, justice, and humility.
**Actively Learn and Apply Wisdom**
Regularly study the Bible and other resources that help you grow in wisdom, and actively apply what you learn in daily life.
**Avoid Temptation and Danger**
Identify potential traps and temptations in life, and actively seek wisdom and guidance to avoid these snares.
**Share Wisdom**
Share your wisdom and learning with family, friends, and community, to help them also avoid danger and lead meaningful lives.
**Develop Decision-Making Ability**
When facing choices, consider carefully and pray for God’s guidance, so as to make wise decisions and avoid actions that bring negative consequences.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for giving us wisdom through Your Word, so that our lives have clear direction. We ask that You help us hold fast to spiritual principles and let them become the spring of our life. Give us strength to avoid every snare that could damage our souls and lives. Inspire us not only to seek wisdom for ourselves, but also to share these precious teachings with others, so they do not go down the road of death. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep seeking and applying the teaching of wisdom in your daily life. May it become a spring in your life, protecting you from danger and leading you toward a brighter and steadier future. May your wisdom deepen, so that at every step you can feel God’s leading and protection. Amen!

v: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
b: This passage reminds us that in life there are two entirely different attitudes: one is thinking we are always right, the other is being open to the guidance and advice of others. Wise people are always ready to listen, to learn, and to draw lessons from the experience of others.

A young entrepreneur, when starting his business, was full of confidence and believed all his decisions were right. But he soon ran into difficulty, because the market did not respond as he expected. At this critical moment, a senior entrepreneur reached out a hand to him, offering valuable advice and a new strategic direction. The young entrepreneur decided to put down his pride and listen to the counsel of this experienced mentor. As a result, he not only saved his business, but it began to flourish.

This story shows the importance of wise people’s willingness to listen and accept guidance. Wisdom lies not only in accumulating knowledge and experience, but in recognizing that we do not know everything and learning from others.

In our daily lives, we face countless decisions and choices every day. When we choose to open our minds and listen to different opinions, we not only improve our own ability to solve problems, but also strengthen our relationships with others. True wisdom comes from humbly recognizing that we need the help and wisdom of others.
a: **Actively Seek Opinions and Feedback**
Before making a decision, take the initiative to ask trusted friends, family, or mentors, and listen to their opinions and advice.
**Keep an Open Mind**
Stay open to different viewpoints and new ideas. Even if they differ from your initial thoughts, consider their valid points.
**Strengthen Self-Reflection**
Regularly assess your conduct and decisions, think about how you can improve, and seriously consider the criticism and counsel of others.
**Cultivate a Spirit of Humility**
Admit that you are not always right and that you need the help and guidance of others to reach the best way of living and deciding.
**Learn and Practice Effective Communication Skills**
Learn to listen to others’ opinions and to express your own views effectively. This not only helps resolve disagreement but also builds mutual understanding.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us wisdom and guidance. We ask that You help us humbly accept counsel in our lives and learn to listen to the opinions of others. May our hearts always stay open, willing to learn from every conversation and benefit from the wisdom of others. We ask that You make us humble and teachable people, always growing in Your light. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
#SoulSnack #Wisdom #KingdomAirFellowship
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you always keep an open and humble attitude in life, willing to listen to and learn from the counsel of others. May this wisdom lead you to a brighter and more successful road, and in the process bring more joy and peace to you and those around you. Amen!

v: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
b: This verse shows us that true growth and progress often come from challenging feedback and constructive criticism, not from meaningless praise or empty pleasure. It reminds us to have the courage to face the voices that can help us grow, even though they may sometimes bring discomfort.

A young writer submitted his work for the first time to a veteran editor. His first novel was full of passion and creativity, but it also had many flaws in structure and narrative. The editor’s feedback was strict but fair, pointing out these flaws and offering ways to improve. At first the young writer felt discouraged and misunderstood, but in the end he decided to revise his manuscript according to the editor’s suggestions. After several months of repeated revision, his work was published and highly praised by readers and critics.

This story shows how the rebuke of the wise can become a catalyst for achievement. Compared with the empty praise of fools, such a rebuke does more to help us surpass ourselves and succeed. The rebuke of the wise pushes us forward and lets us learn from our mistakes, so that we reach higher accomplishments.

In our daily lives, whether at work, at school, or at home, we should learn to appreciate those who dare to point out our shortcomings. This feedback, though it may sometimes make us uncomfortable, is an indispensable part of our growth.
a: **Seek the Guidance of the Wise**
When facing major decisions or life challenges, take the initiative to seek out and listen to the opinions and advice of people you respect who have wisdom.
**Learn to Accept Rebuke**
When a wise person criticizes your conduct or decisions, learn to accept it and learn from it, rather than being defensive or denying it.
**Distinguish Constructive Criticism**
Learn to tell constructive criticism from unhelpful rebuke. Accept the former for personal growth, and stay alert to the latter.
**Practice Patience and Humility**
Keep a patient and humble attitude when receiving rebuke, which shows that you are willing to grow and improve.
**Improve Your Own Judgment**
Through continual learning and practice, improve your judgment so that you can better recognize true wisdom.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for teaching and refining us through the rebuke of the wise. We ask that You give us open and humble hearts, so that we can receive and learn from criticism that comes from a voice of wisdom. Help us improve our judgment, to recognize and absorb helpful lessons and avoid being misled by foolish talk. May our lives be brighter and have more direction as we receive Your wisdom. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be brave enough to accept the rebuke of the wise and find chances to grow in it. May these experiences become the cornerstone of your spiritual maturity and personal development. May your ears always be open to the voices that promote your wisdom and understanding, and may you stay far from the songs of fools. Amen!

v: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
b: This passage reminds us that wise reproof is not only precious; it also beautifies and enriches our lives, adding to our radiance like golden earrings and ornaments of fine gold. When we choose to accept and practice these wise words, our lives become more beautiful and meaningful.

A young painter was looking for a breakthrough on his artistic path. Although he was full of passion, he often felt lost in technique and expression. An experienced artist noticed the young man’s struggle and decided to give him some guidance. This senior artist’s reproof was a rare treasure to the young painter; he taught him how to observe light, master color, and boldly express his own feelings.

As time passed, the young painter’s skill improved markedly, and his work began to show his own unique style and depth. Like seeds planted in his heart by wise reproof, his artistic career began to blossom and won wide recognition and praise.

This story tells us that wise reproof is like an ornament of fine gold, increasing not only our outward beauty but, more importantly, our inner worth. When we are willing to listen to and practice such reproof, our lives will be richer and more colorful.
a: **Actively Accept Reproof**
When wise people offer guidance and reproof, open your heart to receive it, and see it as a precious gift that helps personal growth and spiritual deepening.
**Learn to Obey**
Practice an attitude of heeding reproof, not only listening but acting on it, letting these teachings turn into concrete changes in life.
**Cultivate a Humble Mindset**
Recognize that whatever your age or experience, there is always room to learn new perspectives. Humility is the beginning of wisdom and the foundation of continued growth.
**Find Reliable Mentors**
Find one or more trusted wise mentors in your life, talk with them regularly, and seek their guidance and advice.
**Share the Wisdom You Learn**
When you have learned a precious lesson from someone’s reproof, be glad to share that wisdom with others, to help them grow and improve.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us guidance and enlightenment through the reproof of the wise. We ask that You help us keep open and humble hearts, willing to accept and practice these teachings. May this reproof be as precious in our lives as golden earrings, an ornament of our spiritual and moral life. We ask that You guide us to find reliable mentors, and give us opportunities to pass on to others the wisdom we have learned. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your ears always be open to wise reproof, and may these words be treasures in your life, beautifying your days and guiding you along the right path. May every step of yours be lit by the radiance of wisdom, bringing endless blessing. Amen!

v: A wise man has great power. A knowledgeable man increases strength,
b: This passage emphasizes how wisdom and knowledge give us strength, so that we can face the challenges of life and press boldly forward. Wisdom is not only about accumulating knowledge, but about how to apply that knowledge to make wise decisions.

A young engineer was devoted to inventing a new energy-saving technology. His technology had the potential to change the way energy is consumed, but facing complex technical challenges and limited funding, his progress once came to a standstill. Yet the engineer did not give up. He researched deeply and even went back to school for further study to increase his store of knowledge. This new knowledge gave him new ways to solve the problem, and he was able to develop his innovative technology successfully.

This story shows how wisdom and knowledge give us strength to overcome seemingly impossible obstacles. The engineer’s experience proves that a knowledgeable man really can increase strength, and that his effort and determination will in the end bring success.

In the life of each of us, this principle applies as well. Whether we face professional challenges, difficulties in relationships, or the need for personal growth, embracing wisdom and knowledge always makes us stronger and more capable.
a: **Keep Learning and Growing in Knowledge**
Keep increasing your knowledge in your professional field and personal interests. This will not only improve your abilities but extend your influence and your ability to solve problems.
**Apply Knowledge in Practice**
Turn the theory you have learned into action, whether at work or in everyday decisions, and let knowledge be a tool for raising efficiency and effectiveness.
**Share Knowledge with Others**
Pass on your knowledge to others through teaching or sharing sessions. This will not only help them grow, but also reinforce your own learning.
**Encourage Innovation and Creative Thinking**
Encourage yourself and those around you to take innovative approaches to solving problems, so that you can reach your greatest potential when facing challenges.
**Take Part in Decision-Making**
Take an active part in important decision-making processes in your community or workplace, and use your wisdom and experience to have a positive influence on your team or organization.
pr: Dear Lord, thank You for giving us wisdom and knowledge, so that we have the ability to solve problems and make wise decisions in life. We ask that You help us keep learning, increasing in strength, and apply what we learn to real life to improve our effectiveness. Let us be bold to share knowledge, encourage innovation, and take an active part in decisions, guided at every step by Your wisdom. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep growing in strength as you pursue wisdom and knowledge. May this strength not only help you overcome life’s challenges, but also help you grow spiritually and become a more complete and influential person. May you find true strength and courage in the light of knowledge. Amen!

v: Those who are wise will shine as the brightness of the expanse. Those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever.
b: In our lives, everyone hopes to shine, to become a guide and example for others. Today’s verse reminds us that true radiance comes from wisdom, from the pursuit of truth deep within us and a steadfast commitment to justice.

In a small village far away, there was a teacher who taught the children not only knowledge but also how to become people of character and responsibility. His classroom was very special; its walls were covered with photographs of stars and great figures from around the world. At the start of each new term, he would tell his students: “Look, these are people who once shone in their own worlds. They are great not only because of their achievements, but because of their wisdom and courage. You can shine like them too.”

The teacher often said, “Light is not only something we see; it is something we feel. When you study with all your heart and act with love, your life will give off a light that cannot be ignored.” The teacher’s words and actions deeply influenced every child in the village. Years later, these children each shone in different fields, whether as doctors, teachers, or social workers. They all remembered the teacher’s words, and in their own ways lit up the lives of others.

This story tells us that the light of wisdom comes from our thirst for knowledge and our pursuit of truth. When we devote ourselves to leading others to righteousness and showing upright and generous conduct, we not only light the path of our own lives, but also bring hope and light to those who follow us.

Wisdom is like the stars, never fading. In your life, whether through education, acts of love, or an honest daily life, you can become a shining star. Every time you choose justice and choose truth, you are that light of wisdom, lighting up the darkness.
a: **Live Out Truth and Justice**
In daily life, choose to act fairly and sincerely, as the Bible teaches. Whether at work or in relationships, let your conduct be a light that illuminates the road to truth.
**Be a Spiritual Mentor**
Look for opportunities to guide and encourage others, especially those who are seeking direction in life or facing spiritual struggles. Through your words and actions, be a light for them.
**Keep Learning and Growing**
Keep advancing on the road of wisdom and spirituality. Invest time in studying the Bible and joining Bible study groups and seminars, so that your spiritual life is continually renewed.
**Share Your Testimony of Faith**
Through the internet, social media, or at church, share how you have experienced God’s leading and grace, and let your testimony encourage others to seek and rely on God.
**Take Part in Service and Mission**

Take an active part in service activities in your church and community, especially those that can directly change people’s lives, such as food banks, clothing donations, or international mission work.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word that the wise shine like the light of the sky, lighting up this world. We ask that You give us wisdom and courage, so that we can walk in Your light and become that light that leads others to righteousness. Help us show Your love and truth not only in words but in actions. Make our lives a light that never goes out, lighting a world that needs hope. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you shine brightly on the road of wisdom, becoming a starlight that guides others to righteousness, shining on the world forever and ever. Amen!

v: Many will purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined, but the wicked will do wickedly; and none of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.
b: This passage gives us a deep insight: in the refining of life, true wisdom comes from how we respond to and understand these challenges. Wisdom is not only the accumulation of knowledge, but a deep insight into good and evil, right and wrong.

In ancient times there was a king who had a beautiful garden, but it was often damaged by small animals. The king ordered the animals to be captured, but a wise man advised him not to. The wise man said the animals were only following their instincts, and the real solution was to change the layout and plantings of the garden so that the animals would be naturally deterred. The king listened to the wise man’s advice, and as a result the garden was not only free from damage, but more prosperous than ever.

This story inspires us: when facing the trials of life, wise people choose to understand the deeper causes and look for fundamental solutions, rather than blindly dealing with surface problems. Wise people understand that the real answer often requires us to look beyond immediate difficulties and discern the nature of things.

In our own lives, when we face difficulty or challenge, do we choose a short-sighted response or wise reflection? This passage reminds us that choosing the latter will not only take us beyond our present predicament, but let us learn and grow from it, and finally reach spiritual and moral purification.
ah: In today’s verse, we are reminded that wisdom is not merely the accumulation of knowledge, but an understanding and insight into the deeper levels of life. This wisdom can help us keep a pure and clear path in the refining of life, away from the evil deeds of those who are still trapped in folly. Here are some ways to put this wisdom into practice:
a: **Deepen Self-Reflection**
Regularly examine your conduct and motives, and keep your heart pure and clean, as gold is refined in the fire.
**Actively Learn and Grow**
Keep pursuing new knowledge and deeper understanding, especially in spiritual and moral learning, which will improve your judgment.
**Stay Away from Evil Deeds**
Learn to recognize the temptations and traps in daily life that can lead to evil deeds, and actively look for ways to avoid those situations.
**Extend Your Influence**
Use your wisdom to influence and help others, especially those struggling morally and spiritually. Through guidance and support, help them gain deeper understanding and change.
**Hold Firm Convictions**
Find strength in your faith, so that even in challenges and trials you can stay firm and pure, as pure as gold that has gone through the refining fire.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us wisdom, so that in this confused world we can keep a clear and pure mind. We ask that You help us keep learning and growing, and stay upright and pure in every trial. Let our lives be an example to others, leading them toward a clearer path. We pray that our wisdom may be like a pure white light, shining on and influencing those around us. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be a wise person in the refining of life, not only purifying your own soul but also gaining growth through a deep understanding of difficulty. May your wisdom be a lighthouse that guides others to light, so that all of us may find truth and peace in the light of wisdom. Amen!

v: The wise will inherit glory, but shame will be the promotion of fools.
b: This saying deeply reveals the connection between wisdom and honor, and the consequence of lacking wisdom. Wisdom is not only the accumulation of knowledge; it is the ability to understand and apply knowledge to make right decisions, and this ability finally brings a person honor.

Take the architects of ancient Greece, who designed many works of architecture that still amaze the world today. These architects were able to create timeless works of art because they not only mastered the techniques of building, but also knew how to live in harmony with nature and how to balance function and beauty in a building. It was this wisdom that let their works stand the test of time and win endless honor.

On the other hand, imagine a business leader who pursues only quick success and status. He may rise quickly in his career, but lacking true wisdom and moral sense, his success soon turns into an object of public criticism and shame. Such examples tell us that a rise without wisdom can only end in failure and shame.

In our daily lives, this passage encourages us to pursue true wisdom. This includes not only learning and accumulating knowledge, but, more importantly, learning how to apply that knowledge to influence and improve our own lives and the lives of others. Only then can we truly gain honor, and keep our dignity and self-respect when facing challenges.
ah: Today’s verse teaches us that wisdom brings not only knowledge but true honor and respect in life. The lifestyle and decisions of wise people reflect careful thought and the pursuit of noble values; by contrast, however high a fool rises, in the end he cannot escape the shame that comes from lacking wisdom. Here are some ways to practice wisdom and so gain true honor:
a: **Keep Learning and Improving Yourself**

Keep pursuing new knowledge, not only academic knowledge but a deep understanding of human nature, morals, and ethics. This helps us make wise choices in complex relationships and professional decisions.
**Integrity and Honesty in Conduct**
Hold to integrity and honesty in all your conduct; this is a core mark of wise people. Upright conduct will naturally attract respect, rather than false outward show.
**Reflect and Apply Wisdom to Daily Decisions**
Every time you make a decision, think it through and consider its long-term effects. Applying wisdom can make life smoother and avoid needless mistakes.
**Teach and Inspire Others**
Sharing your wisdom and experience not only helps others grow, but is itself an expression of honor. As a spreader of wisdom, you will gain deep inner satisfaction and the respect of society.
**Stay Humble**
True wisdom goes with humility; wise people know they are always learning. Humility keeps us clear about our own limits and respectful of others’ views and abilities.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word the truth that wisdom brings honor. Give us hearts that keep pursuing wisdom, so that Your teaching shows in our daily lives and decisions. Help us gain the respect and honor of others through lives of integrity, honesty, and humility. Enable us to put the wisdom we have learned into real life, not only improving ourselves but encouraging and lifting those around us. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true honor in the pursuit of wisdom. May every step you take reflect the wisdom in your heart, so that your life is not only successful but dignified and worthy of respect. May your wisdom be your radiance, lighting your path and leading you to true honor. Amen!

v: A fool vents all of his anger, but a wise man brings himself under control.
b: This passage shows us the deep connection between wisdom and self-restraint. It tells us that true wisdom lies not only in having knowledge, but in being able to control our emotions, especially in the face of challenge and pressure.

A teacher met an especially mischievous student in class. The student not only did not do his homework, but often disrupted the order of the class. In such a situation it would have been easy for the teacher to lose her temper, but she chose a different approach. She decided to take a deep breath first, and then talk calmly with the student, trying to understand the reason behind it. In this way she found that the student was doing poorly because of family problems and a lack of confidence. The teacher’s patience and understanding in the end helped the student improve his behavior and make progress in his studies.

This story shows the power of the wise holding back their anger. When we choose patience over haste, we not only keep our inner peace, but may open a new way to solve the problem. Wise people understand that outbursts of anger often only make a problem worse, while calm allows us to see the solution clearly.

In our lives, every day brings moments that make us want to lose our temper. But if we can learn to control our emotions like the wise, we can not only solve problems more effectively, but also set an example among those around us, influencing them to face their own challenges in a more positive way.
ah: In Proverbs 29:11, we learn that the wise and the foolish are fundamentally different in how they handle anger. The wise can control their emotions, while the foolish let anger control them. Here is how we can put this teaching into practice in daily life and grow into wise people who hold back their anger:
a: **Develop Emotional Self-Awareness**
Recognize the ups and downs of your emotions, understand what triggers your anger, and learn to notice the signs before your emotions erupt.
**Practice Deep Breathing and Calming Techniques**
When you feel anger rising, try taking deep breaths, stepping away briefly from the situation, or meditating. These methods can help you calm down and avoid impulsive behavior.
**Use Nonviolent Communication**
Learn nonviolent communication skills, using the format “I feel... when... because...” to express your feelings and needs rather than blaming the other person.
**Seek Understanding Rather Than Reaction**
When you are in conflict with someone, first try to understand the other person’s position and feelings. This can help you assess the situation more objectively and reduce anger.
**Build Positive Coping Mechanisms**
Find healthy ways to deal with anger, such as exercise, journaling, or talking with a trusted friend.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us in Your Word that wise people can control their anger and not let emotion rule their behavior. We ask that You give us the ability to exercise self-control, so that when we face challenges and conflict, we can respond with a peaceful and wise heart. Help us learn effective communication and emotion-management skills, so that in any situation we can stay calm and respectful. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you learn to stay calm in the face of pressure and challenge, and manage your emotions like the wise. May your self-control be a source of your strength, leading you toward a brighter and more successful future. Amen!

v: so as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;
b: This passage is a gentle reminder to us that we should actively seek wisdom and knowledge, and devote our whole hearts to this pursuit. True wisdom is not gained by accident; it requires us to consciously open our minds and focus on the people and experiences in life that can teach us.

In ancient Greece, a young man longed to become a great philosopher. He heard that a certain wise man lived on a distant mountain, so he resolutely set out on a journey to find wisdom. When he finally found the wise man, the wise man told him, “True wisdom is not in the answer you seek, but in all that you learn in the process of seeking it.” The young man began to understand that the true meaning of wisdom lies in listening, learning, and understanding the language of the world around us.

This story reflects the importance of “turning your ear to wisdom” that Proverbs speaks of. Each of our lives is full of opportunities to learn, whether from the advice of others, the knowledge in books, or the experience of daily life. When we see these opportunities as precious learning resources, our lives will become richer and more meaningful.

So when we face challenges and decisions, let us learn to stop and listen to the voices of wisdom that can guide us. Whether from teachers, friends, family, or even seemingly unremarkable everyday conversations, we can draw wisdom and increase our understanding and discernment.
ah: Proverbs 2:2 encourages us to “turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding.” This is not only a call to wisdom but an art of living, requiring us to actively pursue depth and understanding. In this fast-paced world, learning to listen and reflect is a precious ability. Here are concrete steps to help us put this teaching into practice in daily life:
a: **Set Aside Regular Quiet Time to Learn**
Set aside a time each day, whether morning or evening, to focus on learning and reflection. This can be reading the Bible, philosophy books, or any material that promotes thinking.
**Take an Active Part in Discussion**

Join a study group or discussion group and exchange insights with others. In these discussions, learn to listen to other people’s views and think deeply about how they fit with your own understanding.
**Practice Meditation**
Practice meditation, deepening your understanding of life through inner stillness. Meditation helps clear the noise from the mind, so that we can hear the voice of wisdom more clearly.
**Record and Reflect**
Keep a habit of journaling, recording what you learn and what inspires you each day. Writing helps organize your thoughts and deepen your understanding, and is a bridge between learning and practice.
**Thirst for Knowledge**
Keep your curiosity and desire for knowledge, whether in your professional field or personal interests. This longing will drive us to keep pursuing deeper wisdom and understanding.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us in Your Word to turn our ear to wisdom and apply our heart to understanding. Give us a heart eager to learn and ears that are sensitive, so that in this noisy world we can hear Your voice and the call of wisdom. Help us put what we learn into practice in daily life, gaining not only knowledge but depth and richness in life. We ask that You guide us on the path of wisdom, and make our lives more complete and meaningful. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you listen closely and give your full attention on the road of seeking wisdom. May this wisdom be a light in your life, guiding you through every difficulty, so that in any circumstance you can make wise choices. May your soul keep growing in the pursuit of understanding, and your life bloom with the radiance of wisdom. Amen!

v: My son, let them not depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion,
b: This passage is a deep reminder, emphasizing the importance of wisdom and discretion, and teaching us always to stay focused on and guard these precious resources. Wisdom is not only the accumulation of knowledge and information, but the ability to apply that knowledge to real life; it guides us to make wise choices and avoid danger and failure.

It is as if you hold a bright lamp in your hand, lighting your road as you travel at night. This lamp stands for wisdom and discretion. If you carelessly let it out of your sight, or neglect its importance, you may get lost or fall in the dark. Wisdom likewise is an indispensable guide on our journey through life; it helps us find direction, avoid mistakes, and reach our destination safely.

The importance of wisdom and discretion can also be seen in the sailors of ancient times. These sailors used the stars to navigate. Their wisdom lay in knowing how to read the night sky, and their discretion lay in how they set their course on the basis of that knowledge. If they never let that knowledge out of their sight for a moment, they could successfully cross unknown seas.

In our lives, every decision, every choice, and every relationship we handle requires wisdom and discretion. Whether making strategy at work, resolving conflict in family life, or even in personal growth and self-reflection, wisdom is an indispensable tool.
ah: Proverbs 3:21 teaches us to “keep sound wisdom and discretion, and don’t let them depart from your eyes.” This passage emphasizes the importance of continually pursuing wisdom and discretion and staying alert to them. In our daily lives, here are some concrete ways to practice this teaching:
a: **Continual Learning and Self-Improvement**
Actively seek new knowledge and keep educating yourself. Whether through books, online courses, or attending seminars and lectures, continual learning helps us stay sensitive to knowledge and wisdom.
**Practice Reflection**

At the end of each day, take time to reflect on the day’s experiences and what you learned, and consider how to apply the wisdom you have newly gained to real life. This habit can help us better understand and absorb what we learn.
**Share Wisdom**

Share your knowledge and wisdom with those around you. This not only helps them grow, but is also a process of deepening your own understanding. Teaching others is an effective way to test and strengthen your own knowledge.
**Stay Alert and Careful**
When facing everyday decisions, always stay alert and use wisdom and discretion to guide your choices. This involves not only the big decisions of life but small daily choices as well.
**Cultivate a Wise Perspective**
Develop the habit of looking at problems from many angles, which can help us understand situations more fully and form more effective strategies.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us in Your Word to keep sound wisdom and discretion at all times. Give us a passion for continual learning and growth, so that we can keep improving ourselves and let Your wisdom guide our lives. Help us put what we learn into daily life and pass Your wisdom on to others, so that we may be lights of Your love and truth. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you always keep sound wisdom and discretion, treasuring them as the light before your eyes. May this wisdom and discretion be a fixed star in your life, not only guiding you through difficulties and challenges but lighting the road ahead. May you, while keeping wisdom, also keep discovering new insights and chances for growth in your life. Amen!

v: who stoops down to see in heaven and on the earth?
b: Imagine the Master of the universe, who not only created the vast galaxies, the mountains and the valleys, but also chooses to look down on our small lives and care about every little joy and sorrow of ours. Such humility comes not from weakness, but is an expression of immeasurable power and love.

A successful entrepreneur had reached the peak of his career and had all the wealth and status people dream of. But one day he saw a janitor in the park working hard, with no one paying attention. The entrepreneur decided to put down his pride, and every morning began to help the janitor for an hour, just to listen to his story and share his work. This action changed his view of life, and he learned true humility: not looking down from a height, but walking alongside on level ground.

Just like our Lord, who though seated on high, chooses to be with us, watching and taking part in each of our days, we too can imitate such humility. At work, we can choose to talk with colleagues as equals, rather than being arrogant. At home, we can listen patiently rather than rushing to give orders. In the community, we can serve others and share our time and resources.

Humility is not only worship of God; it is also a way to connect with others, bringing deep relationships and true self-knowledge. When we learn to lower ourselves, we find life full of new opportunities and joy.
ah: Peace to you, dear family. Let us follow together today’s Soul Snack action guide. Today we will think about and practice the message of Psalm 113:6: “who sits enthroned on high, who stoops down to see in heaven and in the earth?” This verse shows us that even though God Himself sits on high, He still chooses to humbly attend to the affairs of the world, great and small. As His people, we should also imitate God’s humility. Some ways to put it into practice in daily life include:
a: **Listen to Others**
In conversation, give others more attention and time, and learn to truly understand their needs and feelings.
**Serve Others**
Look for opportunities to serve in the community, whether volunteer activities, helping neighbors, or caring for family members.
**Recognize Your Own Limits**
Admit that you are imperfect, and learn to humbly accept advice and criticism in your work and relationships.
**Avoid Arrogance**
When you achieve something, stay modest and thank those who helped and supported you along the way.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we ask that You help us learn Your humility, so that in daily life we may pay more attention to others, serve our communities, and learn with humble hearts. Make our hearts more like Yours, always thankful and far from pride. Thank You for Your guidance and protection in our lives. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true freedom and peace in learning humility. Amen!

t: The Lord Is Humble in Heart
v: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
b: In our busy lives, pressure often rests on our shoulders like a heavy yoke, leaving us breathless. We look for all kinds of ways to be relieved, yet we often overlook the simplest and most effective answer: humbly following the example of Jesus.

An old farmer used an old ox to plow his field. Though the ox was old, because of its experience it could pull the plow steadily and firmly. One day the farmer decided to pair a young ox with the old one to work together. At first the young ox kept resisting and wanted to go its own way, but it soon learned to follow the old ox’s pace, and together they finished the task with ease. This story teaches us a precious truth: when we choose to humbly learn from and follow a guide wiser than ourselves, our burdens become light.

This is exactly what Jesus invites us to do in this verse. When we choose to take His yoke and learn His gentle and humble heart, our lives will not only become lighter, but our souls will find true rest. This is not only a religious doctrine but a way of life, which lets us stay peaceful and joyful when facing difficulties and challenges.

Let us apply this lesson in our daily lives. Whether in family relationships, work pressure, or personal challenges, when we choose to lay down self and humbly accept instruction, we begin to experience true freedom and peace. This is what Jesus hopes for; He not only gives us direction, but also gives us strength.
ah: Jesus said in Matthew 11:29, “Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.” This verse shows us that true rest comes from humility and gentleness of heart. Here are some ways we can practice Jesus’ attitude of humility in daily life:
a: **Take the Initiative to Serve Others**
In your family, workplace, or community, look for opportunities to serve others. This might be helping a colleague finish a hard task, or caring for neighbors and friends.
**Stay Gentle in Conflict**
When you meet disagreement, strive to stay peaceful and respond with gentle words, avoiding harsh or aggressive language.
**Admit Mistakes and Limits**
When you make a mistake or meet a setback, have the courage to admit it and look for a chance to improve. This self-knowledge is the core of humility.
**Avoid Boasting**
When you achieve something or do well, stay modest and share the glory with those who supported you.
**Seek God’s Will in Daily Decisions**
When facing a choice, first pray and seek God’s guidance, rather than relying only on your own understanding and preferences.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us, through the example of Jesus Christ, to be gentle and humble in heart. Give us strength and wisdom, so that we can learn and practice these virtues in daily life. Help us reflect Your love and humility in every act of service, every conflict, and every decision. May our lives bring rest and encouragement to others, and may all the glory be Yours. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find rest and strength for your life in humility and gentleness. Amen!

v: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the LORD require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
b: In our daily lives, how can these simple instructions become a guide for our conduct? There was an ordinary school teacher who worked in a busy and highly pressured school environment. This teacher chose every day to practice justice, mercy, and humility, even when students did poorly or there was conflict among colleagues. He always treated every student fairly, used a heart of mercy to understand the stories behind them, and stayed humble, learning from every challenge and never thinking himself the best.

This teacher’s story inspired the whole school community. His students learned how to treat others justly, they learned to sympathize with and help classmates in trouble, and they learned to grow from mistakes rather than be arrogant. Through his daily conduct, this teacher not only changed his own life, but influenced those around him.

When we think about our own lives, can we find such moments too? When we face family difficulties, work pressure, or injustice in the community, can we still hold to acting justly, showing mercy, and staying humble? This is God’s call to us, not only the mark of a believer, but the responsibility of a human being.

Let us set out from here today, walking with God with hearts that act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly, and practice these eternal truths in our lives. When we do, we will find not only that our lives are more harmonious, but that our relationship with God is deeper.
ah: In Micah 6:8, we are reminded of the conduct Yahweh expects: to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God. This is not only a call to do good, but a blueprint for daily life. Here are some concrete ways to practice this verse:
a: **Act Justly**

In daily life, whether at work or in personal relationships, always hold to integrity and fairness. This may mean standing up courageously in the face of injustice, or staying honest in small matters.
**Love Mercy**
Actively look for opportunities to show compassion and sympathy. This can be offering help to someone in trouble, or paying attention and responding to the needs of those around you.
**Walk Humbly**
Stay modest and not arrogant when you interact with people. Learn to listen to others’ opinions, respect different views, and admit your own shortcomings and mistakes.
**Walk with God**
In daily life, keep seeking God’s guidance and wisdom. This includes keeping a close relationship with God through prayer, meditation on the Bible, and taking part in church activities.
**Reflect and Adjust**
Regularly reflect on whether your conduct fits these principles, and make adjustments when necessary. This self-assessment helps us keep growing and improving.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for clearly showing us through Your Word what is good. We ask that You give us strength and wisdom, so that we can act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with You in life. Help us practice these teachings in our daily conduct, not only for our own spiritual growth, but also so that we can make a difference in this world that needs hope and light. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. As you act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly, may you draw nearer to God each day and enjoy every step of walking with Him. Amen!

v: You pronounced judgment from heaven. The earth feared, and was silent,
b: In a world full of change and challenge, this verse gives us great comfort and hope. It reminds us that however unsettled the world around us may be, God’s justice and salvation always guard the humble.

There is the story of an old woman who in her life went through many hardships and misfortunes. She lived in a small village in poverty, and was often oppressed by the local powerful. Yet she always kept a humble and kind heart, firmly believing that God would reach out a hand to help.

After an extreme act of injustice, things turned around. A judge from far away visited her village and heard her story. Deeply moved, the judge decided to step in and investigate, and finally brought justice for her and the other villagers. This not only changed the old woman’s life, but brought the whole village an unprecedented peace and fairness.

This story shows us that even in seemingly helpless circumstances, an attitude of humility and integrity can draw help from heaven and become a force that changes destiny. As the Psalm says, God arises to save the humble, and when they need it most, He brings them justice.
When we face injustice or challenge in our own lives, let us remember this lesson. Stay humble, and trust in God’s justice and promises; He will surely give us strength and deliverance.
ah: Psalm 76:8 gives us a far-reaching insight, reminding us that God will rescue the humble and show justice in His judgment. It teaches us that whatever challenge or injustice we meet in life, holding to a humble heart is the key to being saved by God. Here are concrete ways to practice this biblical truth:
a: **Keep Examining Yourself**
Assess your thoughts and conduct every day, making sure they stay in line with God’s will. When you realize you have strayed from the path of humility, repent at once and seek God’s guidance.
**Service and Giving**
Look for opportunities to serve in your community and church, especially unseen service, such as helping the vulnerable, or doing things that seem small but are actually very important to others.
**Learn Patience and Yielding**
In conflict and pressure, choose to respond with humility and understanding rather than haste or arrogance. This not only solves problems but is a concrete way to live out humility.
**Put Others’ Needs First**
In making decisions, first think of others’ needs and feelings and put yourself second. This is a concrete practice of humility.
**Stay Humble Through Prayer**
Keep communion with God, asking through prayer for a humble heart, and for God’s peace and joy to remain with you in daily life.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word that You will save those who are humble in heart. Help us practice humility in our daily lives, whether in our words, conduct, or decisions. Keep our hearts in line with Your heart, and let us rely on Your strength when facing the challenges of the world. We ask that You give us a humble spirit, so that we grow in Your grace and become witnesses of Your love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you be saved by God in humility, and at every step of your life feel His presence and peace. Amen!

v: When they cast down, you will say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.
b: These words give us a deep insight: in adversity, when the world tries to pull us down, God has set a higher calling for us. This is not only a test of our faith but a divine assurance that our future is not decided by the people or circumstances around us, but by the almighty God.

Bamboo needs five years to build its root system in the soil, and during that time you can hardly see any sign of growth. But once it begins to grow, bamboo can shoot up as much as 90 feet in just six weeks. This is like the seasons of humility in our lives: it may seem that there is no progress, but in fact we are building a solid foundation for explosive growth.

Think of the great scientists, artists, and even business leaders who were misunderstood or underestimated; their stories have proved this truth many times. For example, Thomas Edison met countless failures in his early experiments, yet never gave up. Each failure was, for him, a chance to take another step toward success. His humility and perseverance finally led him to invent the electric light, which changed the world completely.

Now, when we face challenges or are put down, let us remember Edison’s perseverance and the growth of the bamboo. These stories not only inspire us, but remind us that in God’s plan, every humble beginning lays the road to prominence.
ah: Job 22:29 gives us a powerful message: even when others bring us low or we suffer injustice, the humble can hold on to hope, because God promises to save the humble. Here are concrete ways we can practice this teaching in daily life:
a: **Stay Steady in the Face of Humiliation**
When you meet criticism or humiliation from others, keep your mind steady and calm, not shaken by outside negativity.
**Learn to Let Go and Forgive**
Do not cling to past hurts; learn to forgive those who may have made you feel put down. This is not only an expression of humility but the beginning of inner freedom.
**Seek God’s Help in Difficulty**
When you feel pressed down or beset by difficulty, pray actively to God, seeking His help and guidance.
**Live Justly and Uprightly**
Even when underestimated, strive to do what is right and keep your conduct in line with your faith.
**Receive Lessons with a Humble Heart**
Every low point is a chance to learn and grow. Accept these lessons with a humble heart and let them lift you.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word that even when we are brought low, we can keep hope, because You promise to save the humble. We ask that You give us strength and wisdom, so that when we face challenges and injustice we can still keep a humble and upright heart. Help us learn to forgive, and to rely on You in difficulty, trusting that You will lift us to a higher place. May we show our faith in and dependence on You at every step of life. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you keep growing in humility, and may almighty God save and lift you. Amen!

v: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.
b: This verse shows us a very beautiful promise: for those who keep a humble heart, God will not only guide them but also teach them to walk the right path. Humility is not only a realistic assessment of our own abilities, but also an acknowledgment of, and trust in, God’s all-knowing and all-powerful nature.

A teacher, in teaching her students, noticed that the students who were most receptive to knowledge and guidance were often those with a humble attitude who were willing to listen. These students trusted the teacher’s wisdom and experience and were willing to follow her guidance, and in the end learned more and achieved better grades.

This is very similar to our relationship with God. When we stay humble in spirit, recognize our limitations, and seek God’s guidance, we open ourselves to the road of God’s wisdom. Just as the teacher guides her students, God will lead us to a more right and just path.

This principle applies not only to our personal lives but also to our careers and relationships. When we meet difficulties and challenges and humbly seek God’s guidance, we will find ourselves able to respond to every situation more wisely, and to learn precious lessons from it.
ah: Psalm 25:9 reminds us that God will guide the humble and teach them His way. This is a beautiful promise to those who keep humble and open hearts to seek God’s guidance in life. Here are concrete ways we can practice this teaching in daily life:
a: **Cultivate a Humble Mindset**
Take the initiative to look for chances to learn and grow, admit that you do not know everything, and seek others’ opinions and advice.
**Seek God’s Wisdom in Decisions**
Before every important decision, seek God’s guidance through prayer and meditation on the Bible, to make sure your choice is in line with God’s will.
**Practice Patience and Long-Term Obedience**
In following God’s will, be patient, and keep holding to God’s teaching even when you cannot see obvious results or benefits right now.
**Show Humility by Serving Others**
Humility also shows in how we treat others. Practice humility by helping and serving those in need; this is not only doing good, but a way of learning and practicing God’s way.
**Keep a Humble Attitude of Learning**
At work, at home, or at church, accept each day’s experiences as a learner, and see every moment of life as a chance to learn from God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for promising through Your Word to guide the humble and teach them Your way. Help us develop a humble heart, seek Your guidance in our daily decisions, and practice Your teaching in every area of life. May we reflect our faith in You and dependence on You in every moment of service, learning, and living. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you receive God’s guidance and teaching in humility, and grow each day in His justice and love. Amen!

v: The LORD upholds the humble. He brings the wicked down to the ground.
b: This verse reveals an extremely important truth: in God’s kingdom, humility is not weakness but a source of strength. When we put down our pride and accept God’s will with a humble heart, God Himself becomes our support and strength.

Think of an old bridge bearing a heavy load, weathered by years and seeming ready to give way. Yet the reason the bridge can keep carrying its load is not that it is unbelievably strong, but that its structure lets it bend under pressure without breaking. This is very much like our lives. When we stay humble under the weight of life, we are in effect allowing God to carry those burdens, so that we are not broken.

A young entrepreneur faced enormous financial pressure when his start-up was in trouble, and many expected him to fail. But he chose not to rely on his own wisdom; he sought deeper spiritual guidance and humbly accepted help from outside. It was this humble attitude that brought him key support, which not only helped him through the crisis but eventually took his business to new heights.

This story shows us that whatever the challenge, humility can open for us the door to support and success. As the Psalm says, when we choose humility, God will uphold us and bring down the troubles of the proud.
ah: Psalm 147:6 emphasizes God’s special care for the humble and His judgment on the wicked: “Yahweh upholds the humble. He brings the wicked down to the ground.” This verse not only encourages us to stay humble in daily life, but also assures us of God’s support for those who act humbly. Here are some concrete ways to help us practice this teaching:
a: **Be Brave Enough to Admit Your Limits**
At work and in relationships, when you are unsure or need help, have the courage to admit it and ask for others’ opinions and help.
**Give Glory to Others and to God in Success**
When you achieve something, remember to share the credit with those who supported you and with God, recognizing that your achievement is the result of teamwork and God’s grace.
**Take an Active Part in Service**
Look for opportunities to offer selfless service at church or in the community. By helping others, you not only show humility, but personally experience God’s support for the humble.
**Practice Humility in How You Treat Others**
In every situation, treat others with humility and respect, even those who seem lower in status or less capable than you.
**Stay Humble in the Face of Criticism and Difficulty**
When facing criticism or unfair treatment, accept it with a humble attitude, look for chances to grow in it, and trust that God will bring justice at the right time.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word the importance of humility, and for promising to uphold the humble. Help us practice humility in every part of daily life, whether in handling success or in facing challenges. May our hearts always seek Your glory, and not only our own interests. In our humility, may we feel Your support and guidance. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find God’s support in humility, and stand firm in every trial. Amen!

t: God Gives Grace to the Humble
v: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
b: In our lives, this passage reminds us of a basic but vital principle: God favors those whose hearts are humble, and resists an attitude of arrogance. This message is not only spiritual teaching; it is also a practical guide for living, telling us how to act with the right heart so as to receive God’s grace.

Think of how a seed sprouts and grows in the soil. The seed itself must first break open and give up its original form, which is a posture of humility. Only when the seed is willing to open itself can it take in the nutrients around it and gradually grow into a flourishing tree. This process shows the power of humility: it is not weakness, but the beginning of growth and of receiving more grace.

We can see the real-life meaning of this principle in the story of a famous scientist. Early in his research career, this scientist faced major challenges and failures. Yet he did not choose to cling proudly to his own theories; he chose to humbly listen to the criticism and advice of his peers. It was this humble attitude that finally let him break through his difficulties and make a pioneering scientific achievement, which won honor for himself and brought blessing to the whole world.

This story encourages us that, whether on our career path or in daily life, when we choose humility rather than pride, we open for ourselves the door to receiving God’s rich grace. Humility lets us learn, grow, and accept guidance, while pride closes off these channels.
ah: James 4:6 reminds us, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.” This verse stresses the importance of keeping a humble heart, and promises that the humble will receive God’s abundant grace. Here are some concrete ways to practice humility in daily life and receive God’s grace:
a: **Self-Reflection and Self-Knowledge**
Regularly take time to reflect on your conduct and attitudes, and check whether there is any pride or complacency. Assess yourself honestly and ask God’s help to improve.
**Practice Humility in Your Interactions with Others**
Whether at work, at home, or at church, respect others’ opinions and feelings, and listen sincerely rather than rushing to give your own view.
**Pray for God’s Guidance and Grace**
In prayer, ask God to give you a humble heart, and ask Him to guide you in every area of life, so that you rely on Him rather than on your own strength.
**Accept Setbacks and Learn to Grow from Them**
When you meet failure or challenge, accept these experiences with a humble heart and see them as chances to grow and learn, rather than reasons for self-denial.
**Service and Giving**
Practice humility by serving others selflessly. When you turn your attention from yourself to others and help those in need, your humility will naturally grow.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word of the importance of humility. We ask that You help us practice humility in daily life, in our thoughts, words, and actions. Let us often examine ourselves and show a humble attitude in our dealings with others. We ask that You give us the grace that comes from You, so that in every challenge and opportunity we can rely on You and grow in Your love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength in humility, and live, grow, and prosper in the grace of God. Amen!

t: The Spirit of the Humble Revived
v: For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
b: In this verse we witness a profound truth: God not only dwells in the high heavens, but also comes down Himself to live with those who are contrite and humble in spirit. This is a beautiful promise to those who seek renewal and revival in spirit and heart.

There was a dry land, which had not seen rain for a long time and was cracked all over. After a timely rain, the land was thoroughly soaked, life was restored, and plants began to sprout. Like this land, a soul that has gone through hardship and drought can also be renewed and revived after receiving God’s presence and grace.

This teaching is an encouragement to everyone facing challenge and hardship. Take an old man who hit a low point in life and was disheartened by illness and loneliness. Yet when he needed it most, he chose to pray to God and seek help rather than sink into despair. By humbly accepting support and love from the community, his spirit was gradually revived, and he found again the courage and purpose to go on living.

This story reminds us that whatever difficulty we face, when we choose to lay down self and humbly seek grace from God, our souls and hearts can be revived and strengthened. God promises to be with us, just as He is with all who are contrite and humble in spirit.
ah: Isaiah 57:15 gives a deep insight: God dwells not only in the high and holy place, but also among those who are contrite and humble in spirit. His presence is meant to revive the spirit of the humble and renew the heart of the contrite. Here are concrete ways to practice this teaching in daily life:
a: **Cultivate a Contrite Heart**
Often reflect on the gap between your conduct and God’s will, and sincerely repent of your sins and shortcomings. This attitude brings us closer to God and brings us His renewal and grace.
**Keep a Humble Way of Life**
In your dealings with people, humbly put others before yourself, whether in listening or in offering help. Humility lets us serve others better and reflect the love of Christ.
**Keep Your Relationship with God Through Prayer and Devotion**
Regular prayer and devotion are not only for seeking God’s guidance, but also for joining our spirit with God’s Spirit, letting God’s Word fill our hearts and renew our minds and souls.
**Seek Spiritual Unity in Community**
Grow together with brothers and sisters in the church and in faith groups, sharing testimonies and encouraging one another as you seek spiritual revival together.
**Live Out a Humble Witness**
